papers.title: Does the direct anterior learning curve persist after fellowship training? A single-center comparative cohort study
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction : The direct-anterior-approach (DAA) for total hip arthroplasty (THA) has significant benefits but has historically been associated with a steep learning curve. However, modern training in the approach may eliminate that learning curve. We hypothesize that newly graduated surgeons with specific training in the DAA would show no difference in complication rates compared to senior DAA surgeons. Methods : This retrospective cohort study included 600 primary THAs performed via a DAA from a single institution between November 2019 and February 2025 with a minimum of 90-day follow up. Intra- and post-operative complications were compared between the following two groups: the first 100 cases of each of three junior fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeons (“Junior”) and the most recent 300 cases of a senior fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeon (“Senior”). Results: The incidence of operative complications was low and showed no significant difference between groups (Junior − 30 (10.0%) vs Senior − 23 (7.7%), p = 0.39). Subgroup analyses showed no between-group differences for DVT (1.3 vs 0.7%, p = 0.686), PE (0.7 vs 0.3%, p = 1.000), hematoma (0.3 vs 1.0%, p = 0.62), dislocation (1.3 vs 0.3%, p = 0.37), periprosthetic fracture (1.7 vs 1.0%, p = 0.73), neuropraxia (1.3 vs 2.0%, p = 0.75), prosthetic joint infection (1.0 vs 0.3%, p = 0.62), or wound complications (2.3 vs 2.3%, p = 1.00) (Table 2). Medical events were infrequent, with a non-significant trend toward more events in the Senior cohort (Junior − 7 (2.3%) vs Senior − 14 (4.7%), p = 0.181). Operative time was found to be longer among Junior surgeons (92.3 vs 68.5 minutes, p < 0.0001). No difference in patient reported outcome measures (PROMs) were found at 90 day follow up between junior and senior surgeon cohorts. Conclusion : The results of this study suggest that while fellowship-trained DAA surgeons starting practice have longer operative times, there is no difference in overall complication rates or patient-reported functional outcomes when compared to a Senior DAA surgeon. This demonstrates that the historical learning curve surrounding adoption of the DAA may not apply with exposure to the approach during adult-reconstruction fellowship training.

papers.title: Hydrogel Formulation Containing PLGA Nanoparticles for Controlled Codelivery of Vitamin D and Chlorhexidine as a Promising Approach for Postdental Implant Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Tooth loss can have a significant impact on oral health and quality of life, and dental implants are currently the standard option for its replacement. However, implant failure still occurs, with bacterial infection and inadequate osseointegration being the most common causes. In this context, vitamin D3 was selected for its known pro-osteogenic role, while chlorhexidine (CHX), a widely used antiseptic with recognized bactericidal and bacteriostatic activity, was chosen as the antimicrobial component. To enable controlled and localized delivery of both molecules, two types of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles (NPs) were developed, CHX- and vitamin D3-loaded NPs. The produced NPs displayed an average size of 140 nm, a polydispersity index below 0.2, and negative ζ-potentials. Encapsulation efficiency reached 39% for CHX and 98% for vitamin D3, and transmission electron microscopy confirmed their spherical morphology. In vitro release assays demonstrated an initial burst release followed by a slower release phase for 3 days under simulated physiological conditions, while stability tests under storage conditions showed preservation of the nanoformulations’ physicochemical properties for at least 2 months. Antibacterial assays against Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and Staphylococcus epidermidis (S. epidermidis) confirmed the antimicrobial effect of CHX-loaded NPs. Cytotoxicity studies in human dermal fibroblasts indicated that combining both formulations (50 nM vitamin D3 and 0.01% w/v CHX) was safe. To facilitate application in the oral cavity, the NP mixture was incorporated into a nontoxic, pseudoplastic hydrogel. These findings highlight the potential of this nanohydrogel as a localized therapeutic approach capable of providing localized antimicrobial activity and supporting conditions favorable to osseointegration, paving the way for improved long-term implant outcomes.

papers.title: Latent RL Priors for Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from limited visual demonstrations is challenging because policies must acquire both perceptual grounding and precise control, while reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation can acquire rich control behaviors from large-scale interaction with privileged information. We introduce \textbf{Latent RL Prior}, a two-stage framework that reuses this control knowledge for data-efficient visual policy learning. During privileged pretraining, we distill large-scale RL rollouts into a flow-matching action decoder conditioned on proprioception and latent task context. During visual adaptation, we freeze the decoder and learn a visual interface that maps images to its latent context using action supervision alone, without privileged labels or latent targets. The same decoder can further be shared across arms by learning coordinated visual contexts for bimanual manipulation. Across three simulated tasks, our method outperforms full-parameter fine-tuning of $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 in the low-data regime; on door lifting and bimanual assembly, it surpasses full-data baselines using $10\times$ and $5\times$ fewer demonstrations, respectively. Further analysis shows that direct visual-to-latent conditioning improves adaptation performance and training stability over routing visual predictions through the pretrained state encoder. Robustness to unseen mass variation and greater linear accessibility of contact-force information in decoder representations further provide evidence of retained RL-acquired control knowledge. Project website: https://yixiaowang7.github.io/latent-rl-prior-page/.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction for Time-Dependent PDEs
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification is crucial in scientific machine learning, where models inform safety-critical tasks such as flood forecasting, financial risk management, and thermal control in machines. Conformal prediction provides distribution-free coverage guarantees, but in time-dependent settings common to physics and engineering, these guarantees can break down, leading to systematic undercoverage. We study this problem in the context of surrogate models for time-dependent physical systems described by partial differential equations. We prove that in a function space setting, distributions at arbitrarily close times can be mutually singular, making exact coverage guarantees impossible. We further show that in discretized settings, the total variation distance between distributions often saturates exponentially fast with the grid resolution, mandating restrictions on the spatial discretization to ensure coverage. Finally, for certain settings, we show how to use principled weighted conformal prediction to obtain finite-sample coverage guarantees over growing time horizons.

papers.title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
papers.abstract: Designing healthcare strategies requires anticipating their clinical and operational consequences before implementation, a task that often relies on health system simulation. Such a simulation necessitates modeling how patient states evolve and generate care demands. However, conventional approaches typically tailor compact state transitions to a single policy question and omit history-dependent dynamics, thus requiring the redefinition of states and transitions when there is a new question that entails different clinical information. We propose to learn a patient world model from longitudinal EHRs using a neural network to provide a shared clinical representation of patient trajectories that can serve simulation questions across scenarios. Taking ICU operations as an example, we train the model on MIMIC-IV, freeze it, and couple its time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues via scenario-specific mappings, so that one model renders admission demand, care tasks, and discharge proposals across simulations evaluating ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity. Experiments show that our model matches Markov and semi-Markov comparators in aggregate occupancy and directional responses to capacity and dispatch policies. It also reproduces policy gains from replayed observed trajectories. For patients entering the same support state from different prior trajectories, the learned representation captures a 24-h recovery difference (-6.4 predicted versus -6.7 observed percentage points), a contrast missed by compact state models, which propagates into distinct simulated care demand, queue burden, and bed use. These results indicate that a learned world model of patient dynamics has the potential to replace question-specific state models, allowing new care policies to be evaluated by reconfiguring the scenario without model rebuilding.

papers.title: SHORE: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Online Bin Packing
papers.abstract: Online 3D bin packing with a processing buffer requires choosing which box to pack, its orientation, and its placement while keeping the stack stable under unknown future arrivals. A collapse ends the episode and forfeits the remaining volume. Existing methods use geometric rules or hard stability masks, limiting how risk can influence the joint choice of box, orientation, and placement. We propose Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning (SHORE), which combines a learned stability probability of a placement with an on-policy estimate of its return conditional on stability. A 3D U-Net learns stability from executed outcomes and simulated alternatives, revealing outcomes of actions underrepresented in early rollouts. A discrete on-policy actor--critic uses stability predictions in both its action values and policy prior, with gates that limit the effect of an untrained or changing model. In deployment, SHORE does not require additional search or simulation overhead. In Isaac Gym, SHORE reaches 73\% space utilization by 0.4M environment steps, while the same learner without stability modeling reaches that level at about 1M. On the expanded 60-box set, SHORE achieves 0.734 space utilization versus 0.588 for the GOPT state-of-the-art baseline, with a higher placement-failure frequency (1.03\% vs. 0.63\%), trading more risk for greater packed volume. The results show faster learning and higher utilization on the more demanding realistic box arrival set. Ablations suggest that simulated alternatives provide useful early supervision, while executed outcomes alone sustain later performance. We also demonstrate the method on a real robot to verify the simplicity of integrating the method to real bin packing pipelines.

papers.title: GPWM: Modeling the World as 3D Particle Motion
papers.abstract: We introduce GPWM, a Generative Particle World Model that predicts how 3D scenes evolve by generating the motion of particles and rigid bodies over time. Unlike video world models that generate scene appearance, GPWM operates directly in 3D physical space. A single representation and architecture cover rigid, deformable, cloth, and granular materials, in both passive physics and robotic interaction. GPWM is an object-aware multi-resolution transformer that combines flow matching with diffusion forcing to generate coherent physical trajectories far beyond its training horizon. We train and evaluate GPWM on ParticleWorlds, a 25.5-million-frame corpus spanning diverse geometries, materials, interactions, and robot embodiments. GPWM outperforms the best prior learned-dynamics baseline in each of six physical domains, reducing prediction error by 31% on average. Breaking from the domain-specific setting of prior methods, a single Unified GPWM models these heterogeneous regimes with one set of weights, largely outperforming per-domain baselines and even surpassing our own specialist models in two domains. GPWM further generalizes to unseen geometries, physical properties, object counts, and rollout horizons. Beyond prediction, GPWM enables contact-rich planning by learning a generative prior over joint actuator-object motion. Instead of searching over unconstrained actions, planning searches the model's latent noise for interactions that achieve a desired object-space goal. With the same world model, noise-space planning substantially outperforms action-space search on pushing and picking, where complex contact sequences are hard to discover. Executed open-loop in simulation, the resulting plans achieve goal-directed manipulation without reference action trajectories or goal-specific policies.

papers.title: FreeOcc: Decoupling Ego-Motion for Efficient 4D Occupancy Forecasting via Continuous Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Current 4D occupancy world models use heavy cross-attention or deep recurrence to disentangle ego-motion from scene dynamics. This requires significant computational capacity. However, this effort is largely redundant since the ego-vehicle's intended future motion is provided by the downstream motion planner. We present FreeOcc, a lightweight continuous-time world model that introduces explicit $SE(2)$ geometric decoupling into a conditional flow-matching framework. By mathematically factoring out self-motion, we create a purely dynamic feature space. This space supports attention-free temporal fusion and allows physics-constrained ODEs to operate strictly on residual agent kinematics. To maximize deployment efficiency, FreeOcc introduces an uncertainty-aware blending mechanism. This routes well-observed voxels to a single-pass decoder, reserving the ODE solver exclusively for ambiguous, high-uncertainty regions. Requiring only 28.3M parameters-roughly 40% of comparable models-our optimal ensemble mode (FreeOcc-E) runs at 27 FPS. On nuScenes, FreeOcc achieves state-of-the-art forecasting performance with a 0.47 m Near Field Chamfer Distance (NFCD) and 32.1% mIoU. Furthermore, the model transfers zero-shot to SemanticKITTI. It also proves highly robust, retaining 92.8% of its ideal mIoU under significant sensor packet loss and timestamp jitter.

papers.title: Identifying Neural Dynamics Using Nonlinear Interventional State Space Models
papers.abstract: State-space models (SSMs) recover low-dimensional latent dynamics from high-dimensional observations, but latents are generally not identifiable from observational data alone. Interventional state-space models (iSSMs) use perturbations to break observational symmetries and identify parameters up to permutation, scaling, and shift. However, prior work restricts identifiability to linear latent dynamics and piecewise-linear emissions, excluding many behaviors characteristic of neural circuits. We extend iSSMs to a substantially broader model class: we prove that (i) affine identifiability holds under general injective emission functions and Gaussian latent transitions, and (ii) with interventions, identifiability up to permutation, scaling, and shift is preserved under general nonlinear latent dynamics. We validate our theory on simulated FitzHugh-Nagumo dynamics, and then demonstrate two applications: adjudicating between competing models of decision-making; and predicting responses to unseen micro-stimulation in macaque and human neural recordings, with proof-of-concept generalization to a held-out stimulation site in the latter. Finally, simulations yield practical guidance for designing stimulation protocols that improve identifiability.

Within its basic Fourier neural operator architecture, spectral weights are expressed as continuous functions of normalized radial frequency through a learnable sum of Gaussians. This representation preserves the geometric properties of the lithography system and incorporates rotation and translation equivariance, spatial interaction decay, and direct evaluation on different layout windows. Experiments predict aerial images from mask layouts and resist images from aerial images, demonstrating the geometric equivariance and spatial adaptivity of LithoSAGE. Comparisons with other architectures also assess prediction errors and parameter efficiency.

WAM-Sim structures persistent context across three temporal and semantic scales: pose-aligned structural tokens encoding persistent road topology, read-only scene tokens supplying geolocated background appearance, and write-once instance tokens preserving individual traffic participant identities across occlusions and chunk boundaries. To restore visual sharpness and physical plausibility degraded by multi-scale conditioning, we introduce an online post-training framework that optimizes self-generated rollouts via flow-matching RL guided by hierarchy-aligned visual rewards and a vision-language model physical judge. The invariant memory empirically confines policy optimization within the anchored context, helping suppress semantic collapse and reward hacking, while online RL systematically enforces physical commonsense and fine-grained visual fidelity. On the nuScenes benchmark, WAM-Sim achieves a superior generation fidelity (FID=3.47, FVD=25.72) and strong downstream perception performance (24.16 mAP, 71.23 road mIoU). On minute-scale rollouts of self-collected data, WAM-Sim substantially mitigates structural and identity drift, preserving high scene similarity and subject identity coherence across extended horizons. Our framework constructs each objective as differentiable energies on the sampler's intermediate clean-action estimate, which needs only forward access to the frozen model, and is stabilized by sampling-time guidance scheduling, per-energy normalization, and velocity-bounded correction. On the NAVSIM v2 hard-split, guidance improves all three frozen, publicly released WAMs by 1.8 to 3.6 EPDMS, averaged over three sampler seeds, and adds less than 10% to the sampling time per step. These results position energy guidance as a practical post-training control channel for WAMs.

papers.title: TactileLab: Sim-to-Real Dexterous Robot Manipulation with Efficient Shear-Sensitive Tactile Simulation
papers.abstract: Robotic simulators that represent shear within tactile sensing are becoming increasingly important for contact-rich manipulation. However, simulating contact shear with high-fidelity deformable or soft-body simulation is computationally demanding, limiting scalability to large-scale reinforcement learning. Here we introduce \textit{TactileLab}, a scalable multimodal tactile simulation framework built on IsaacLab, with a particular focus on a new optical-flow-based tactile representation termed \textit{simulated tactile flow}. Instead of relying on soft-body physics to model shear deformation, TactileLab uses rigid-body simulation to efficiently estimate dense tangential motion at the contact interface, producing tactile flow fields that encode shear-relevant contact dynamics. This flow field complements geometric features from a contact depth field. We further introduce a novel policy architecture for jointly processing long-horizon proprioceptive signals and rich tactile observations. Across multiple contact-rich tasks, policies trained using simulated tactile flow learn efficiently at scale and exhibit emergent contact-aware behaviours. To facilitate sim-to-real policy deployment, we then propose a novel real-to-sim tactile translation method that maps real tactile image streams to simulated tactile flow and depth fields, together with a new tactile data collection method, and validate it across diverse tactile sensor designs. Using this pipeline, we demonstrate real-world deployment on tasks encompassing dual-arm and dexterous in-hand manipulation. Overall, TactileLab provides an end-to-end sim-to-real framework for scalable tactile policy learning, enabling diverse shear-sensitive manipulation across heterogeneous tactile robotic systems.

papers.title: PlayGen2: Learning Real-Time Playable Worlds with Explicit 3D State
papers.abstract: Building a playable world requires more than generating plausible video: it demands responsive control, persistent spatial structure, and coherent interactions with dynamic entities. Using generated frames as the sole recurrent world representation ties these requirements to view-dependent appearance synthesis, making it difficult to maintain long-term spatial and temporal consistency in generation and interaction. We present PlayGen2, a real-time interactive world model that separates learned 3D state evolution from neural rendering. PlayGen2 maintains a persistent world memory comprising static geometry represented by a volumetric occupancy grid and identity-indexed 3D states for the player and other entities. Within a fixed-size local region, its world-state model jointly learns action-conditioned entity dynamics, geometry completion, and entity discovery, committing updates to a persistent world memory. A separate neural renderer synthesizes first-person observations from depth and semantic projections of the world state, without feeding generated images back into state prediction. Using Doom as a testbed, we demonstrate that the model successfully learns world dynamics including geometry-aware player motion and player--NPC interactions. The framework is computationally efficient, enabling the complete simulation and rendering pipeline to achieve approximately 160ms backend latency on a MacBook Pro with an M4 Pro chip. Beyond single-player interaction, we demonstrate zero-shot deployment on unseen Doom maps, multiplayer interaction through the composition of single-player models, and programmable gameplay through rule-based state interventions. These capabilities demonstrate the transferability and extensibility of the learned game-world model. Code and pretrained model weights are publicly available.

papers.title: Online Optimization for Controlling HVAC Systems
papers.abstract: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems account for a significant portion of buildings' energy consumption, motivating the design of energy- and cost-efficient control strategies. However, conventional strategies employ simple, reactive control, without incorporating a model. Therefore, in this paper we adopt an economic model predictive control framework and focus on designing online algorithms to solve the control input design problems with a limited computational budget. In particular, we propose two tailored online algorithms based on projected gradient descent, with a custom projection routine, and the projected primal-dual method. We discuss the pros and cons of both algorithm designs, focusing in particular on computational efficiency. We further compare them through numerical experiments simulating the control of an HVAC system over the course of a day. The results show that computationally efficient online solvers for HVAC systems control are indeed possible. Moreover, the performance closely matches that of a baseline algorithm with unlimited computational budget, in terms of reference temperature tracking and comfort temperature range enforcement.

papers.title: Seeing Beyond the Next Step: World-Model-Guided Human-Like Navigation in Multi-Agent Scenes
papers.abstract: Selecting a next motion in a populated scene is not just a matter of avoiding what is currently in the way: an action can be locally feasible yet drift onto the road instead of the crosswalk, cut into a stream of crossing pedestrians, or bottleneck a narrow passage. These failure modes are invisible from the current state alone, and acting on them requires reasoning about what each candidate action will cause. World models offer exactly this, namely action-conditioned predictions of the future, but rolling them out at every decision step is a cost deployable navigation systems cannot pay, and the field has largely traded foresight for speed. We argue this is a false dichotomy. The natural place for a world model in human-aware navigation is at training time, as a preference oracle that distills foresight into a fast policy, rather than at inference time, as an online planner. We pair a discrete visual action prior with two task-aligned world models, one for nearby social dynamics and one for future scene semantics, that score candidate actions by their predicted consequences and refine the policy through group-relative preference distillation. At deployment, both world models are removed and the policy acts in a single forward pass. Across five held-out evaluation scenarios, this yields navigation that is simultaneously safer, more socially and group-coherent, and more goal-directed than strong reactive and learned baselines, with naive observers rating the resulting motion as more human-like. Taken together, our findings point to a different approach for bringing world-model foresight into deployable agents: not accelerating rollouts, but amortizing them into the policy so that the cost of looking ahead is confined to training. papers.title: Simple Meta-Learning for HPO and CASH Using Performance Representations
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization for Hyperparameter Optimization (HPO) and Combined Algorithm Selection and Hyperparameter Optimization (CASH) often relies on explicit hyperparameter encodings as surrogate inputs. In high-dimensional search spaces, however, such representations can make it difficult for standard surrogates to learn useful performance models. We instead study an alternative meta-learning representation that describes each configuration directly as its historical performance across prior tasks. This representation can be paired directly with standard surrogate models. Our scope is the iterative selection component of AutoML, deciding which configuration to evaluate next from a fixed candidate set, rather than a complete framework with features such as runtime estimation, cost-aware budgeting and ensembling. We further apply this representation to maximal marginal relevance (MMR), a diversity-based re-ranking criterion from recommender systems, as a posterior-free acquisition rule. When selecting and optimising across multiple models on the TabArena benchmark, the performance-based representation paired with a linear Bayesian ridge regression model outperforms dedicated meta-learning baselines, achieving the same tuned performance in roughly half the number of trials. For single-model HPO, it remains a competitive second. Across both benchmarks this method closely matches or improves on regret at a fraction of the complexity and cost, requiring no pre-training or tuning and scaling independently of search space dimensionality. Code for reproducing our results is available at https://github.com/EWitting/simple-metalearning.

papers.title: Two-stage residual learning for calibrated uncertainty in solar irradiance forecasts
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting of renewable generation requires not only point predictions but also reliable estimates of the uncertainty attached to them, particularly at extended horizons. Machine learning models are increasingly used to predict solar output, but they typically report a single value and capture the associated uncertainty poorly. The standard remedy is to train a model to predict the parameters of an assumed probability distribution directly. Here we develop an alternative two-stage method, motivated by synthetic solar signal generation, in which the forecast error is modeled separately from the expected irradiance. A first long short-term memory (LSTM) network predicts the expected global horizontal irradiance, and a second network models the distribution of the forecast error, which is added back to the mean to give both the forecast and its uncertainty. Using historical weather data from the National Solar Radiation Database and a probability integral transform evaluation, we show that explicitly modeling the error brings the predicted standard deviation markedly closer to the historical value, reducing the deviation between the two by 34.6 percent for a standalone LSTM and by 56.5 percent when the LSTM is coupled to Gaussian process regression, the most reliable of the configurations tested. Because the method models the total forecast error directly, it captures the full predictive uncertainty that matters for decisions, rather than only the model contribution that dropout-based approaches estimate.

papers.title: Dynamic Watermarking and Action-Conditioned Latent Dynamics for Secure Vision-Based Controllers
papers.abstract: Replay attacks are difficult to detect in vision-based control systems because previously recorded observations can remain plausible while the physical system follows a different trajectory. This paper develops an adaptive dynamic-watermarking framework for detecting replay attacks against vision-based controllers. A private Gaussian watermark is added to the nominal control input, and a control input-conditioned latent dynamics network (LDN) predicts the corresponding evolution in a compact latent space learned from image observations. Attack evidence is obtained from the discrepancy between the predicted latent response and the latent representation of the received image observation. A reinforcement learning policy adjusts the watermark covariance using the latent state and detector confidence, thereby balancing attack detectability, watermark energy, and control distortion. A Lagrangian penalty on task-specific safety costs is included during training to limit the adverse effect of the excitation. The framework is evaluated on a vision-guided UR5 manipulation task in which the robot reaches a target while avoiding a moving human arm under nominal and replay-attacked observations.

papers.title: Changepoint localization via nested exchangeability tests: from point estimates to confidence intervals
papers.abstract: We study distribution-free uncertainty quantification for a changepoint estimate in an offline setting. We observe a sequence with a single changepoint and are given an estimate of its location. The pre- and post-change segments are independent and each consists of i.i.d. (or, more generally, exchangeable) observations from arbitrary and unknown distributions. We introduce Changepoint LOcalization via Nested Exchangeability testing (CLONE), a novel method for constructing distribution-free confidence intervals around that estimate by testing exchangeability in nested windows centered at the reference estimate. Under these assumptions, CLONE provides finite-sample coverage for any black-box reference estimator. Using a geometrically shrinking radius grid, CLONE requires only $O(log n)$ permutation tests. We characterize optimal scores for the framework and provide practical recommendations that result in sharp confidence intervals. Under mild assumptions, CLONE confidence intervals have asymptotically vanishing normalized length. Simulations and experiments on image and text data support our theoretical findings.

papers.title: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: Kinetic equations in the high-field regime describe particle transport dominated by electric-field acceleration and collisional relaxation. These equations are widely used in simulations of plasmas and semiconductor devices. Typical models include the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Boltzmann--Poisson systems. Their high dimensionality and multiscale nature pose two of the major challenges to accurate and efficient numerical solution. To address these challenges, we propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network (APTNN) method. Specifically, to reduce high-dimensional computational costs and memory requirements, we adopt the canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition structure of TNNs to approximate their solutions. We show that the equation residuals retain this decomposition form, allowing high-dimensional loss integrals to be evaluated through combinations of one-dimensional integrals. The resulting computational and storage costs are reduced from exponential to polynomial growth with dimension. To improve the prediction accuracy in the high-field limit, we enhance the baseline AP loss by incorporating the first moment equation. The added loss term directly constrains the limiting flux closure to reduce its approximation error in the high-field regime. The enhanced AP loss can still be evaluated dimension-wise. Numerical results show that APTNN improves prediction accuracy in the high-field regime with significantly reduced computational costs and memory usage. For a 3D3V VPFP problem with multiple random inputs, training takes less than 30 minutes on a single GPU.

papers.title: CRISP: Constraint-Resolved Interactions between Subsystems for Predictive Whole-Body Cooperation
papers.abstract: This paper presents a layered control framework that recasts high-dimensional system dynamics as a composition of dynamically interconnected subsystems, with dynamic dual-arm manipulation on the humanoid serving as a representative application. The humanoid is decomposed into a single rigid body (SRB) representing the torso and floating-base dynamic models representing the articulated arms and lower-body. The rigid connections between arm and torso and the closed kinematic chain formed between the end-effectors during cooperative manipulation are represented as holonomic constraints. The corresponding Lagrange multipliers parametrize the interaction wrenches transmitted at the shoulders and between the end-effectors. The high-level nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) jointly optimizes the subsystem state trajectories, arm torques, ground reaction forces (GRFs), and interaction wrenches, enabling online wrench design and optimization while preserving the dynamic coupling among the independently modeled subsystems. The optimized arm torques are applied directly for cooperative dual-arm manipulation, whereas the prescribed GRFs are mapped to lower-body joint torque for whole-body coordination. We validate the proposed framework through numerical simulations and hardware experiments on a G1 humanoid robot. The results demonstrate optimal interaction wrenches consistent with simulated contact measurement, cooperative dual-arm trajectory tracking, and stable whole-body coordination while executing the NMPC in online manner.

papers.abstract: Deformable linear object (DLO) manipulation is challenging because high-dimensional configurations, nonlinear contact dynamics, and diverse material and geometric properties produce a broad range of object responses that are both difficult to model and data-intensive to learn. This work studies reinforcement learning for planar manipulation of a one-end-grasped DLO, focusing on training efficiency, observation design, robustness, and zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. We compare three Proximal Policy Optimization training stacks and find that the GPU-parallel MuJoCo Playground stack enables faster convergence and more consistent performance than CPU-based alternatives under the same wall-clock budget. Relative keypoint observations and an asymmetric actor-critic formulation further improve learning efficiency. Policies trained with observation noise, delay, domain randomization, and disturbances achieve simulation success rates of 96.4% for single-point tracking, 98.0% for disturbance recovery, and 88.8% for two-point tracking. Using markerless RGB-D keypoint estimation, the policies transfer without real-world fine-tuning, succeeding in 9/10, 10/10, and 8/10 physical trials, respectively.

papers.title: Microstructure evolution and mechanical performance optimization of 30CrMnSiNi2A steel processed by laser powder bed fusion combined with heat treatment
papers.abstract: In this study, 30CrMnSiNi2A high-strength steel components were successfully fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) technology. The microstructure evolution was effectively tailored by the control of laser energy density, which can be adjusted by the laser processing parameters, including laser power, scanning speed, hatch spacing and scanning layer thickness. The effects of laser energy densities on the molten pool morphology, densification, phase constitution and mechanical properties of as-built samples were systematically analyzed. It can be found that when the laser energy density reached 96.2 J/mm3, a maximum relative density of 99.4% can be achieved, while the corresponding microhardness, yield strength (YS) and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) reached 478.3 HV, 1560 MPa and 1159 MPa, respectively. Notably, compared with the mechanical properties of traditional castings reported in earlier studies, these performances were enhanced by 75%, 20.9%, and 46.8%, respectively. Particularly, the scanning layer thickness exhibited the most significant impact on the mechanical properties. This was primarily ascribed to the transition of melt pool from the conduction-dominated regime to the stable keyhole conduction mode at higher laser energy density, where can effectively enhance wetting and remelting to suppress the defect formation and improve the material integrity. During the LBPF process, the retained austenite was gradually transformed into martensite, while the reduced layer thickness can enhance the melt pool fluidity to promote the formation of flat and uniform scanning tracks, and the densification and mechanical performance can be improved. The melt pool boundaries and structural inhomogeneities can be further eliminated by the subsequent heat treatment, leading to the grain growth of austenite phase. After heat treatment, the average microhardness (411.8 HV) and UTS (1341 MPa) were decreased, whereas the elongation was enhanced from 10.1% to 16.1%. Meanwhile, the fracture mode was also shifted from mixed brittle-ductile fracture to ductile fracture. It is anticipated that the fabrication of 30CrMnSiNi2A component with high density and superior mechanical properties can provide a theoretical and practical foundation for the high-performance manufacturing of complex high-strength steel parts in the fields of aerospace and automotive industry.

papers.title: Metal ion levels in well-functioning and failed metal-on-metal bearings in hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Whole blood cobalt testing is widely used in surveillance of metal-on-metal (MoM) hip arthroplasty, but clinically validated reference values for well-functioning implants are not well defined, and modest elevations are often misinterpreted as pathologic. This study aimed to establish outcome-validated cobalt ranges and evaluate their use in distinguishing adverse wear-related failure (AWRF) from trunnion corrosion failure (TCF). Methods We analyzed early (1 to 5 year) cobalt levels in MoM hip resurfacing arthroplasty (HRA) and total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients with confirmed implant survivorship at 10 and 15 years, and compared these to cases that failed due to AWRF, TCF, and other causes. AWRF and TCF classification was based on intraoperative and imaging findings independent of ion results. The influence of implant design and postoperative activity level was also assessed. Results Mean cobalt in well-functioning unilateral HRA was 1.2 ± 1.2 µg/L; all successful implants had levels below 14 µg/L. All 18 AWRF cases had cobalt levels of 15 µg/L or higher (mean 74.0 ± 47.0 µg/L), a clean separation from successful implants. TCF cases (n = 7) showed only modest cobalt elevation (mean 5.3 ± 2.0 µg/L) that overlapped substantially with successful implants, and a definitive diagnostic threshold for TCF could not be established given the small cohort. Activity level did not significantly influence early ion levels. Conclusion Cobalt levels below 14 µg/L are consistent with normal MoM bearing function, while levels of 15 µg/L or higher strongly suggest AWRF. Ion testing reliably identifies bearing-related wear failure but is not diagnostic for TCF, which requires additional clinical and imaging correlation. These outcome-validated thresholds may help reduce unnecessary revision surgery and improve MoM surveillance.

papers.title: Lymphoedema is an independent risk factor for complication after total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Introduction: Lymphoedema is a chronic disorder characterised by the abnormal buildup of lymphatic fluid, most commonly present in the lower extremities. A paucity of literature exists regarding the impact of lymphedema on outcomes following primary total hip arthroplasty (THA). Therefore, we sought to examine the rates of 90-day complications and 2-year revision free survivorship in patients with and without lymphoedema undergoing THA. Methods: Patients undergoing THA for osteoarthritis between 2009 and 2020 were identified from a national administrative claims database. Those with preoperative lymphoedema were then identified and propensity score matched (1:1) to contemporaries without lymphoedema. Exclusion criteria included bilateral THA, patients under 18, and those with less than 90-day follow-up. 90-day complication rates and 2-year revision free survivorship were then assessed with standard statistical methods. Results: 270,180 patients undergoing THA were identified, of which, 1957 (0.72%) had lymphoedema. Analysis of matched cohorts revealed that patients with lymphoedema had higher rates of 90-day deep vein thrombosis (6.6% vs. 3.2%, p < 0.001) and readmissions (10.0% vs. 8.2%, p = 0.016). At 2 years, lymphoedema was associated with an increased risk of septic revision (HR = 1.55, p = 0.020), but no increase in all-cause or aseptic revision rates. Conclusions: Preoperative lymphoedema is an independent risk factor for increased rates of 90-day deep vein thrombosis, and readmissions in patients undergoing primary THA. Importantly, the association with increased septic revision procedures is a cause for concern. Our results highlight the need for aggressive counselling and preoperative optimisation in patients with lymphoedema who are indicated for THA.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence assisted multiobjective design of functionally graded materials using hybrid optimization and experimental validation
papers.abstract: Designing functionally graded materials (FGMs) through conventional trial-and-error approaches is time-intensive and difficult to scale for large multi-material design spaces. This study presents an AI-assisted, computational-intelligence-based framework for compatibility-aware material selection and gradient-profile optimization of FGM structures. The framework combines a curated database of 180 candidate materials with a mixed-variable hybrid genetic algorithm–particle swarm optimization approach to balance weight, cost, stiffness, strength, and thermal resistance. Rapid objective-function screening was followed by finite element verification of shortlisted designs and proof-of-concept experimental validation using powder-metallurgy-fabricated Al₂O₃/Ti-6Al-4V FGM beam specimens. For the representative beam case considered, the optimized FGM showed approximately 25% lower weight, 30% lower deflection, corresponding to approximately 43% higher effective stiffness under identical loading, and 60% lower peak thermal stress compared with the corresponding homogeneous reference under the same modeling assumptions. Experimental measurements from three specimens showed differences of approximately 3% for elastic modulus and 4% for ultimate strength relative to numerical predictions, supporting the feasibility of the workflow for the present case while indicating the need for broader statistical validation. The estimated per-design screening and verification time decreased from approximately 480 h for a conventional trial-and-error route to approximately 18 h after database preparation, although this comparison is case-specific and depends on model fidelity, hardware, and available material data. Overall, the results suggest that AI-assisted multi-objective optimization can serve as a useful decision-support tool for narrowing FGM design spaces before detailed numerical and experimental qualification.

papers.title: Non-thermal argon plasma enhances wettability of Ti-6Al-4V biomaterial surfaces without detectable elemental alteration
papers.abstract: Abstract This in vitro study evaluated whether non-thermal argon plasma could improve the wettability of Grade 5 titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V) surfaces without producing detectable changes in elemental composition. Ninety commercially sourced Ti-6Al-4V discs were allocated to one of three surface conditions: machined, nitric acid-treated, or hydrochloric acid-treated. For wettability analysis, each surface condition was evaluated either without plasma treatment or after 60 s of non-thermal argon plasma exposure at 22 °C, with 13 independent discs per subgroup. Water contact angle was measured using the sessile-drop method, and the mean of the left and right contact angles was used as the specimen-level outcome. Surface morphology and elemental composition were evaluated qualitatively by scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy before plasma exposure and immediately and at 30 and 60 min after treatment. Argon plasma significantly reduced the water contact angle in all surface groups (p < 0.0001), indicating a marked increase in wettability. Mean contact angle decreased from 162.6° to 32.74° on machined surfaces, from 150.5° to 12.96° on nitric acid-treated surfaces, and from 110.0° to 21.87° on hydrochloric acid-treated surfaces. Plasma-treated acid-conditioned surfaces exhibited lower contact angles than plasma-treated machined surfaces. Scanning electron microscopy indicated that plasma exposure made pre-existing topographic features more visually distinct, particularly on acid-treated surfaces, whereas energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy revealed no appreciable changes in elemental composition. These findings support non-thermal argon plasma as a short-term surface-activation strategy for Ti-6Al-4V biomaterials; however, the durability and biological relevance of this effect require further investigation.

papers.title: Microgel-mediated organoid engineering: Biomaterial design, microenvironmental regulation, and biofabrication strategies
papers.abstract: Organoids are organ-like structures formed by the self-organization of stem cells, progenitor cells, or patient-derived cells within a three-dimensional (3D) microenvironment. They are capable of mimicking the cellular composition, spatial structure, and functional characteristics of in situ tissues. Organoids have become an important platform for developmental biology, disease modeling, drug screening, and regenerative medicine. However, current organoid culture remains highly dependent on animal-derived matrices. The poorly defined composition, substantial batch-to-batch variability, and limited tunability of the mechanical and degradation properties of these matrices hinder the clinical translation of organoid models. Microgels typically refer to micrometer-scale hydrogel particles (1–1,000 μm) formed by the crosslinking of natural or synthetic polymers. Compared to traditional bulk hydrogels, microgels combine the design flexibility of individual particles with their collective ability to assemble into larger structures. By adjusting the size, stiffness, porosity, surface ligands, degradation rates, and factor release behavior of microgels, they can provide cells with a more controllable local microenvironment. This review focuses on the fundamental material properties, structural characteristics, fabrication techniques, and functional mechanisms of microgels in organoid engineering. It discusses their applications as cell-encapsulation units, scaffold templates, self-assembling building blocks, and bioactive-factor delivery platforms and evaluates their potential for standardized and scalable organoid manufacturing. Finally, we summarize the key challenges facing the field and outline the future directions for stimuli-responsive microgels, cellular microgelation, pure-cell building blocks, and smart biomanufacturing in next-generation organoid engineering.

papers.title: Multi-level computational framework for assessment of damage evolution in satellite subsystems during launch
papers.abstract: Purpose Main purpose of this research was to set up specialised numerical-experimental approaches for rapid re-design, testing and optimisation of micro- and nanosatellite components to boost new paradigms for faster and less risk-averse space mission developments. Design/methodology/approach The new numerical approach is tailored for rapidly integrated and tested spacecrafts for which critical stress-strain fields and damage mechanisms must be efficiently analysed at various levels and length scales. These range from macroscopic loads imposed by the rocket onto the satellite and its critical subsystems all the way down to damage evolution at micro scales. Findings The applicability of the new experimental-numerical approach has been tested on a real case scenario derived from the first Slovenian microsatellite mission NEMO-HD that required re-design of an optical backend subsystem due to a failure of a joint during pre-launch vibration testing. The proposed approach proved to be excellent for explaining failure causes and justifying applied re-design changes. The derisking approach was found to be very successful because the satellite continues to operate reliably after reaching more than 30.000 orbit cycles in the seventh successful year of remote sensing operations. Originality/value The coupling between the scales is achieved through mesh substructuring and boundary conditions based on the finite element method, while the bridging of scales is facilitated by phenomenological damage mechanics models and a very original implementation of FE2 method where digital twin microstructures for real engineering materials for space applications are homogenised at selected integration points of macro elements.

papers.title: Evaluation of the Effects of Dental Implant Dimension and Design on Primary Implant Stability Using Different Stability Measurement Devices
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Dental implants are an established treatment for functional and aesthetic rehabilitation of partially or completely edentulous patients. This in vitro study evaluates the effects of dental implant design, diameter, length, and bone density on primary implant stability using Osstell ISQ and Penguin Resonance Frequency Analysis (RFA) devices. Materials and Methods: A total of 96 dental implants were included in this study. Combinations of two implant designs (T6 Standard and T6 Torq), two implant diameters (3.5 mm and 5.0/4.8 mm), and two implant lengths (8 mm and 14 mm) were placed into synthetic bone blocks with densities of PCF15 and PCF30. Implant stability was measured twice from two different directions using Osstell ISQ and Penguin RFA devices. The data were statistically analyzed. Results: Both RFA devices demonstrated high measurement reproducibility. When all measurements were evaluated collectively, the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) reached 0.999 for both devices. Bone density was identified as the most influential factor affecting primary implant stability. Significantly higher ISQ values were obtained in the high-density bone model (p < 0.001). Increases in implant length and diameter significantly enhanced primary stability (p < 0.001). T6 Torq implants exhibited significantly higher ISQ values than T6 Standard implants in low-density bone and small-dimension implant combinations (p < 0.001). Conclusions: Under the present experimental conditions, bone density showed the greatest influence on primary implant stability, followed by implant length and implant diameter. In low-density bone, particularly with short and narrow implants, more aggressive implant macrodesigns may contribute to higher primary stability. However, the clinical relevance of these findings requires further investigation.

papers.title: Structure–property relationships in PBF-LB/M AlSi10Mg TPMS lattices: coupled effects of topology, relative density, and heat treatment on compressive behavior
papers.abstract: Abstract Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattices offer strong potential for lightweight structural and energy-absorbing applications, however, the coupled influence of lattice topology, relative density, and post-processing-induced microstructural changes on their mechanical response remains insufficiently understood. In this study, Gyroid, Diamond, Primitive, and IWP AlSi10Mg TPMS lattices were fabricated via laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) at three relative densities and investigated in both as-built and EOS T6 heat-treated conditions. Quasi-static compression testing up to 50% strain was performed to evaluate stiffness, strength, deformation behavior, and energy absorption. While increasing relative density consistently enhanced stiffness, strength, and specific energy absorption, the magnitude and scaling of these improvements were found to depend strongly on topology and material condition. Heat treatment reduced yield strength and peak stress, but also altered deformation behavior and energy absorption characteristics in interaction with the other design variables. The results reveal that the compressive performance of TPMS lattices cannot be accurately described through independent effects of topology, density, or heat treatment alone, but instead emerges from their coupled interactions. This study therefore provides new insight into the structure–property relationships governing additively manufactured TPMS lattices and offers design considerations within the tested parameter space for tailoring mechanical performance through the coupled control of architecture and material condition.

papers.title: Review on modelling of thermoset and thermoplastic composites: constitutive equations, processing modelling and multiphysics modelling
papers.abstract: Abstract Fibre-reinforced composites have emerged as pivotal materials in advanced structural applications across aerospace, automotive, marine, and renewable energy sectors, due to their superior specific strength, stiffness, toughness, recyclability, and rapid manufacturing potential. Composites manufacturing involves complex multiscale, multiphysics phenomena, including melting, crystallisation, flow, fibre orientation, and residual stress generation that significantly influence the final component quality and performance. Process modelling has become an indispensable tool to address these challenges, enabling the prediction of manufacturing-induced defects, residual stresses and dimensional distortion, and reduction of reliance on physical trials. This review examines current process modelling approaches for thermoset and thermoplastic fibrereinforced composites, with emphasis on the constitutive equations, process simulation methodologies and multiscale modelling frameworks used to predict process-induced phenomena. Particular attention is given to predictive frameworks for temperature evolution, crystallinity development, fibre orientation, residual stress generation, and process-induced distortion. Modelling approaches ranging from conventional finite element methods and molecular dynamics to meshless methods and machine-learning-based techniques are critically reviewed and compared with respect to their capabilities, limitations and application domains. Emphasis is given to the integration of process simulation with experimental monitoring and to the transfer of process-induced material states and defects to structural-level performance models. Key challenges that have been identified include uncertainty quantification, computational efficiency, model transferability, and the limited integration of physics-based and data-driven approaches. Future developments are expected to focus on validated multiscale process-structure-performance frameworks, uncertainty quantification, hybrid physics-informed data-driven modelling, and digital-twin-assisted process monitoring to enhance predictive reliability and accelerate the industrial adoption of composite process modelling and simulation.

papers.title: Long‐Term Efficacy of Restricted Quantitative Superior Placement Technique in Total Hip Arthroplasty for Severe Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip: An 8‐ to 10‐Year Follow‐Up of a Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective Total hip arthroplasty (THA) in patients with developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH), particularly those with Crowe II or III dysplasia, is challenging because of abnormal acetabular morphology and deficient bone stock. This study aims to compare the long‐term outcomes of true anatomic versus restricted quantitative superior placement of the acetabular component. Methods This prospective, patient‐ and assessor‐blinded randomized controlled trial was conducted from August 1, 2013, to July 31, 2024. Forty‐four hips were allocated 1:1 to true anatomic center placement or restricted quantitative superior placement. Restricted quantitative superior placement was defined as positioning the cup center no more than 15 mm superior to the true anatomic center. Harris Hip Score (HHS), 36‐Item Short Form Health Survey (SF‐36), complications, perioperative outcomes, and radiographic parameters were assessed. The mean final follow‐up was 8.94 years. Independent‐samples t‐ test, Mann–Whitney U test, Chi‐square test, and Fisher's exact test were used for statistical analysis. Results No statistically significant between‐group difference was observed in prosthetic complications. No revisions were recorded among the 36 hips that completed the 8–10‐year follow‐up. At the 8–10‐year follow‐up, the restricted quantitative superior placement group had a higher HHS than the true anatomic center group (93.70 ± 5.20 vs. 86.73 ± 11.62, p = 0.024); multiple imputation analysis showed a mean difference of 5.79 points (95% CI, 0.46–11.13; p = 0.034). Significant between‐group differences were also observed at 2 and 7 years. SF‐36 scores did not differ significantly between groups. Morselized bone grafting was required in 45.5% of the anatomic center group and 40.9% of the restricted quantitative superior center group. Structural grafting was used in 18.2% and 9.1%, respectively. Radiographic analysis showed higher center of rotation height and less limb lengthening in the restricted quantitative superior center group. Conclusions Restricted quantitative superior placement within 15 mm above the true anatomic center was associated with higher long‐term HHS, with no significant difference in prosthetic complications and no revisions recorded among the 36 hips that completed the 8–10‐year follow‐up. It may represent a potential reconstructive option for patients with DDH. Trial Registration : Chictr.org , ChiCTR‐TRC‐1404388; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=5182

papers.title: Morbid Obesity May be Associated With Increased Odds of Prosthetic Joint Infection After Anterior-Based Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background Obesity increases perioperative risk after total hip arthroplasty (THA), particularly with anterior-based approaches. However, outcomes among patients with class II versus class III obesity remain poorly defined. This study compared early complications and patient-reported outcomes (PROMs) between these obesity classes. Methods We retrospectively reviewed patients with BMI ≥35 kg/m² undergoing elective anterior-based primary THA from January 2022 to January 2025. Patients were stratified into BMI 35-39.9 kg/m² (Class II) and BMI ≥40 kg/m² (Class III) cohorts. Firth penalized logistic regression evaluated the association between BMI group and prosthetic joint infection (PJI) requiring operative irrigation and debridement (I&D). Results 193 patients were included (BMI ≥40: n=53; BMI 35–39.9: n=140). The BMI ≥40 kg/m² cohort had a greater proportion of females (77.4% vs 57.1%; P = .015) and higher ASA classification ( P = .02). PJI occurred more frequently in the BMI ≥40 cohort (7.5% vs 1.4%; P = .049). Unadjusted odds of PJI were higher with BMI ≥40 kg/m² (OR 5.03, 95% CI 1.08-29.6), but the association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for age, sex, and surgical approach. Both cohorts demonstrated significant improvement in WOMAC and SF-12 Physical scores at 3 months without between-group differences. Conclusions Patients with BMI ≥40 kg/m² demonstrated higher observed PJI rates after anterior-based THA while achieving comparable early functional improvement. These findings suggest a clinically important risk signal warranting confirmation in larger studies rather than establishing BMI ≥40 kg/m² as an independent risk threshold.

papers.title: Hybrid Chitosan–BSA Bioinks for DLP Biofabrication and DLP-Assisted Molding of 3D Hydrogel Constructs with Embedded Branched Structures
papers.abstract: Abstract Digital light processing (DLP) bioprinting enables rapid fabrication of high-resolution three-dimensional constructs, but its broader application remains limited by the availability of bioinks that combine structural stability with biological functionality. Here, we present a hybrid chitosan methacrylate–bovine serum albumin methacrylate (ChiMA–BSA-MA) bioink that integrates the structural support of methacrylated chitosan with the biologically favorable properties of methacrylated bovine serum albumin for DLP biofabrication. The hybrid formulations exhibited shear-thinning behavior, rapid photocrosslinking under 405 nm light exposure, and composition-dependent rheological and mechanical properties suitable for vat photopolymerization. Selected formulations enabled fabrication of free-standing constructs exceeding 10 mm in height while maintaining preserved microscale features. Representative complex geometries and embedded branched structures were successfully fabricated using direct DLP printing together with a complementary DLP-assisted molding strategy. Unlike many existing approaches that rely on extrusion-based bioprinting, support-bath printing, sacrificial templates, coaxial nozzles, or other multistep fabrication procedures, the proposed workflow combines direct DLP printing with a simple secondary molding step using a conventional DLP printer. Biological evaluation demonstrated sustained metabolic activity and cell viability over 14 days. Under chondrogenic differentiation conditions, RT-qPCR showed increased expression of SOX9, COL2A1, ACAN, ELN, COL10A1, and MMP13, indicating induction of chondrogenic and hypertrophy-associated marker expression. Overall, the ChiMA–BSA-MA hybrid bioink provides a versatile platform for DLP biofabrication of tissue models with embedded branched structures, expanding the range of photocurable bioinks available for advanced in vitro tissue engineering applications.

papers.title: Bone Drilling Simulation: Effects of Drill Bit Material on Bone Temperature
papers.abstract: Bone drilling is a critical surgical procedure in orthopaedic, dental, and maxillofacial surgery, during which excessive bone temperature elevation at the tool-bone interface can cause thermal osteonecrosis (bone temperature > 47 °C). The subsequent effects compromise osseointegration and implant stability. Drill coating material could regulate both frictional heat dissipation and mechanical cutting resistance. However, the comparative thermomechanical performance of titanium nitride (TiN), titanium carbonitride (TiCN), titanium carbide (TiC), and diamond coatings across multiple simultaneous drilling responses has not been systematically quantified under designed experimental conditions. A Box-Behnken Design (BBD) comprising 60 finite element simulation runs (15 per coating block, 3 centre points per block) was employed to develop second-order response surface methodology (RSM) models for maximum bone temperature and thrust force. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) revealed that the quadratic model was highly significant (F = 137.79, p < 0.0001), with coating material (D) as the dominant factor (F = 497.40), followed by spindle speed (A, F = 702.67), feed rate (B, F = 412.86), and drill diameter (C, F = 177.92). All three coating-by-continuous-parameter interactions (AD, BD, CD) were insignificant (p > 0.19), which indicates that the thermal advantage of diamond over TiN reveals as a uniform absolute offset independent of continuous parameter levels. Multi-objective desirability optimization identified a diamond coating at 944 rpm, 0.020 mm/rev, and 2.8 mm diameter as the optimal condition (d = 0.981), producing the lowest bone temperature (59.8 °C). These findings provide statistically validated guidance for coating selection and the design of surgical drilling protocols to minimize thermal bone damage.

papers.title: miR-1224-5p modulates SND1 expression and correlates with NF-κB signaling in alleviating systemic inflammatory response syndrome following total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is recognized as the optimal treatment for femoral neck fracture (FNF). However, the inflammatory response triggered by surgical trauma cannot be ignored. This study primarily investigated the functions and mechanisms of miR-1224-5p in systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) following THA. The study comprised 300 FNF patients undergoing THA, of whom 128 developed SIRS after THA. RT-qPCR was employed to quantify miR-1224-5p and SND1 levels. Cell viability was assessed via CCK-8 assay, while inflammatory markers were detected using ELISA kits. The NF-κB pathway activation was evaluated by Western blotting. The binding interaction was validated through luciferase activity and RIP assays. Serum miR-1224-5p levels were decreased in patients with SIRS after THA compared with the non-SIRS group. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) treatment impaired THP‑1 macrophage viability, activated inflammatory responses, and activated the NF-κB signaling pathway. miR-1224-5p mimic improved LPS-induced THP‑1 cell function, while miR-1224-5p inhibitor further suppressed the biological functions of the cells. Mechanistically, SND1 was identified as a direct downstream target of miR-1224-5p, and up-regulation of SND1 partially reversed the protective properties of miR-1224-5p on THP-1 cells. miR-1224-5p may be associated with the post-THA inflammatory response, potentially involving SND1, accompanied by alterations in the NF-κB pathway. However, a strict linear axis or target dependence cannot be concluded from the current data. miR-1224-5p is expected to be a promising biomarker and therapeutic candidate for further investigation. papers.title: Seismic Reliability Analysis of Concrete Arch Dams Incorporating Different Valley Shapes: Using a Surrogate Model
papers.abstract: Concrete arch dams are widely constructed in regions featuring deep valleys and distinctive valley shapes because of their high efficiency and economical use of materials. However, the stability of these structures under earthquake loading requires accurate and comprehensive analyses. Accordingly, this study investigates the seismic reliability of these dams, focusing on the effect of different valley shapes on dam safety in terms of the reliability index (β). The research variables—including the slopes on the left and right sides of the valley, the position of the valley bottom and peak ground acceleration of earthquake have been utilized across various scenarios. In this study, a response-surface surrogate model (RSM) was used to generate explicit functions describing dam behavior, ABAQUS was used for finite element (FE) analysis of the models, and MATLAB coding was employed to implement the methods for estimating the probability of failure and the β index. In addition, the probabilistic seismic response of the dams under different valley-shape conditions was evaluated through implicit dynamic analysis using the Northridge, Friuli, and Trinidad earthquake records at different intensity levels. Examining four valley shapes (i.e., V-shaped, symmetric and asymmetric polygonal, and U-shaped) revealed that valley shape strongly affects stress distribution and seismic load-carrying capacity. Valley shape should therefore be considered a key factor in the design and seismic performance assessment of arch dams. The results also demonstrated that symmetric valleys provide the most suitable sites for arch-dam construction and identified valley-shape asymmetry as the most important factor increasing the probability of failure. Overall, this research represents an important step toward developing simulation-based and probabilistic approaches to the design of earthquake-resistant dams.

papers.title: Bayesian inference of expensive simulators: survey and comparison of design choices
papers.abstract: Abstract We present a survey of approaches to Bayesian inference with simulator forward models, focusing on settings with prohibitively expensive simulators. In this domain, Bayesian optimization-based methods have emerged as the most promising approach. We unify existing methods into a general framework, enabling consistent reasoning about shared algorithmic structure across the fragmented literature. Within this framework, we identify the primary design choices and perform a systematic empirical comparison of their effects on inference efficiency in terms of required simulation budget. A key result of our study is that inference efficiency is often dominated by the choice of surrogate-model response variable, as it directly governs the complexity of the modeled function. Specifically, we demonstrate that the prevalent scalar log-likelihood is a poor response variable, as it discards crucial information. Based on this insight, we introduce the concept of custom \emph{proxy variables}: transformations of simulator outputs engineered to retain more information and provide smoother response surfaces, substantially improving inference efficiency over standard response variables. We provide actionable guidance and a numerically robust Julia package to facilitate practical adoption of Bayesian optimization for simulator inverse problems.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning for predicting the splitting tensile strength of SCM-blended concrete using optimized Gaussian process regression
papers.abstract: Abstract This study develops an explainable machine-learning framework to predict the splitting tensile strength of concrete incorporating supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs), which are widely used to reduce reliance on Portland cement. The analysis used 395 valid mixtures extracted from a global SCM-blended concrete database. Cement, water, coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, fly ash, silica fume, ground granulated blast-furnace slag, and superplasticizer were used as predictors. Predictor relevance was assessed using mRMR, F-test, RReliefF, and Random Forest importance. A broad set of regression algorithms was evaluated in MATLAB Regression Learner using 5-fold cross-validation. Rational Quadratic Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) was the best baseline model, with an RMSE of 0.51 MPa, MAE of 0.34 MPa, MAPE of 10.02%, and R² of 0.85. The GPR model was then optimized using Bayesian optimization, random search, and grid search. All three strategies produced comparable predictive accuracy. Bayesian optimization required the shortest training time and was therefore selected for the final model. The Bayesian-optimized GPR achieved an RMSE of 0.41898 MPa, MSE of 0.17554 MPa², MAE of 0.29095 MPa, MAPE of 8.9%, and R² of 0.89. Relative to the baseline model, RMSE and MSE decreased by 17.85% and 32.48%, respectively. Partial dependence plots and SHAP analysis identified water and cement as the dominant predictors. Higher water content generally reduced predicted tensile strength, whereas higher cement content increased it. The findings demonstrate that optimized and explainable GPR provides a reliable data-driven framework for predicting the tensile performance of SCM-blended concrete and supporting performance-informed design of more sustainable cementitious materials.

papers.title: Stochastic optimal sizing of hybrid energy storage system considering uncertain AGC regulation requirements
papers.abstract: Integrating energy storage systems into thermal power plants offers an effective solution for enhancing automatic generation control (AGC) performance. However, existing research has primarily focused on deterministic AGC regulation commands, which fail to accommodate the inherent uncertainties in frequency regulation requirements. To address this gap, this paper proposes a stochastic optimal sizing scheme for hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs) that accounts for uncertain AGC regulation requirements. First, the conditional generative adversarial network is employed to generate a large set of AGC regulation commands, followed by the hierarchical clustering method to extract typical scenarios. Then, a bi-level stochastic optimization model integrating HESS optimal sizing and frequency regulation strategies is developed. The outer level formulates a multi-objective optimization model that maximizes both the economic benefits and frequency regulation performance to determine the optimal HESS capacity. Based on model predictive control, the inner level optimizes the power allocation among thermal power unit, battery energy storage system (BESS), and supercapacitor energy storage system (SCESS) while incorporating AGC tracking errors and BESS cycle life. Furthermore, the multi-objective particle swarm optimization method is used to solve the outer-level sizing model, and the interior point method is employed to solve the inner-level quadratic programming model. The final optimal solution can be obtained through the alternate iteration between the two levels. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed scheme enhances AGC performance, extends BESS service life by 56.1% and increases the net present value by 7.4%, thereby validating its effectiveness.

papers.title: Model-based graph reinforcement learning for robust cyber-attack defense in active distribution systems with high DER penetration
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a model-based graph reinforcement learning (MBGRL) framework for defending active distribution systems with high penetrations of distributed energy resources (DERs) against cyber-physical threats, particularly false data injection attacks (FDIAs). The proposed approach integrates a learned power-flow surrogate model with a graph neural network (GNN) policy to accelerate convergence, reduce simulator dependence, and capture the spatial structure of distribution networks. Adversarial scenario training further enhances robustness under coordinated load-altering attacks, DER-setpoint tampering, and combined multi-vector FDIAs. Evaluated on the IEEE-123 bus system, the MBGRL framework demonstrates significant improvements over existing methods: it reduces simulator interactions by 54% and training time by more than 60%, while achieving superior operational resilience—lowering voltage violations to 5 (compared with 12 for SAC and 18 for MPC) and reducing active-power losses to 89 kW (compared with 102 kW for SAC and 111 kW for MPC). Although incorporating the surrogate model and GNN introduces additional modeling complexity, MBGRL delivers higher sample efficiency, improves robustness to cyber intrusion, scales effectively with network size, and enables interpretable decision-making. The attention-based GNN structure highlights influential buses during control actions, supporting operator transparency. These results identify MBGRL as a practical and scalable defense strategy for modern DER-rich distribution grids facing evolving cyber-attack risks.

papers.title: Explicit Coordinated Signal Timing Optimization Using Soft Actor–Critic and Model Predictive Control Along an Arterial
papers.abstract: Arterial signal coordination requires coupled decisions on cycle length, phase green times, and offsets in an explicit timing plan. This study presents a modular explicit coordinated signal timing optimization (ECSTO) method for a three-intersection arterial. At each cycle-level decision, a soft actor–critic (SAC) agent selects a common background cycle length and offset corrections for the upcoming cycle. A time–space relationship provides base offsets. Modified model predictive control (MMPC) then allocates phase green times using non-negative, intersection-specific cycle adjustments derived from changes between consecutive offset corrections. It does so without a separately scheduled explicit transition cycle. SAC is trained with a phase-weighted discharged-vehicle reward. System vehicle delay and coordinated-direction space-mean speed are used to evaluate and select policies. Across 1000 common demand scenarios in the simulated arterial, ECSTO had 7.16–11.73% lower aggregate mean system vehicle delay and 5.30–10.19% lower total vehicle travel time than five selected explicit timing-control baselines. These reductions remained statistically significant after Holm adjustment. For coordinated-direction space-mean speed, its mean was significantly below four baselines, illustrating a trade-off between system-wide efficiency and coordinated-direction speed. Ablation results describe differences among four tested timing configurations. Second, a dual-mode obstacle-avoidance controller is designed for two typical hazardous scenarios: underwater obstacles and seabed peaks. Based on obstacle-risk assessment, forward guidance points, and a penalty function, the controller guides the ROV safely around obstacles and enables it to rapidly return to the reference trajectory after completing the avoidance maneuver. Furthermore, the disturbance-observer-based event-triggered mechanism improves computational efficiency while maintaining real-time control performance.
