papers.title: Teaching strategies in higher education in OECD member countries (2021–2025) and their effects on learning, motivation, and competence development: a PRISMA systematic review
papers.abstract: Teaching strategies in higher education have gained increasing prominence in recent years, alongside the expansion of active, collaborative, and technology-supported pedagogies. This systematic review analyzed recent scientific evidence on teaching strategies in higher education institutions across Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) member countries, describing their methodological characteristics and their effects on learning, motivation, and competence development. A structured search was conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, ERIC, and PubMed. Peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2021 and 2025 in English or Spanish, addressing teaching strategies in higher education within OECD countries, were included. Eligibility criteria were defined using the PCC framework; study selection followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines; methodological quality was assessed using MMAT-2018 at the item level, without an overall quality score. Of the 564 records identified, 121 studies met the inclusion criteria and were incorporated into the qualitative synthesis. The findings showed a predominance of quantitative designs, mainly non-randomized studies and randomized controlled trials, complemented by mixed-methods and qualitative research. The teaching strategies were grouped into two main pedagogical families: student-centered active learning and technology-mediated or hybrid learning, together with an intermediate mixed category. Across the three groups, formative assessment and structured feedback emerged as shared pedagogical dimensions rather than as independent strategic categories. Most studies were conducted in European contexts and focused on health sciences, education, engineering, and related fields. These strategies were associated with improvements in academic performance, motivation, engagement, self-regulation, and the development of professional and socio-emotional competences. However, recent evidence remains fragmented by discipline, type of intervention, and assessment method, limiting a comprehensive understanding of their impact on university students. Furthermore, the concentration of studies in health sciences and education restricts the generalizability of the findings to other fields such as engineering, the humanities, and the social sciences. Overall, the evidence suggests that higher education systems in OECD countries are progressively adopting more active, hybrid, and technology-enhanced pedagogical models.

First, a prediction model based on Trend-Residual decoupling and Gate-Aware factors is formulated to achieve precise load forecasting. Second, a morphological identification mechanism is designed to explicitly isolate the slowly varying intervals and the abrupt change intervals of the load. Finally, within the slowly varying intervals, the Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm is introduced for global optimization to provide steady-state anchors for the optimization of subsequent abrupt change intervals; conversely, within the abrupt change intervals, Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control integrating a terminal gravitational mechanism is employed for dynamic tracking, thereby realizing a flexible soft-start for the discrete compensation devices. A shared encoder is used to combine split-conformal prediction with Monte Carlo (MC) dropout, thereby enabling robust uncertainty quantification during battery SOH predictions. papers.title: AlphaNet7: a multi-head physics-informed neural network for latent parameter discovery in variable-order fractional systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Solving high-dimensional inverse problems in variable-order fractional dynamical systems from sparse observations remains a major challenge in scientific machine learning. Standard Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) rely on soft residual penalties, which frequently induce gradient pathologies or encounter conservation discrepancies when applied to non-local fractional operators. To address this limitation, we propose AlphaNet7, a constrained multi-head PINN architecture for the simultaneous inverse identification of compartment-specific, time-varying fractional orders and transmission dynamics. The proposed architecture combines a shared feature-extraction backbone with eight independent prediction heads, jointly inferring multiple latent quantities while implicitly integrating the governing phenomenological equations through a custom autograd-compatible piecewise differentiable explicit fractional forward solver. AlphaNet7 is applied to a seven-compartment nonlinear epidemiological system governed by the non-singular Caputo-Fabrizio fractional operator. From two macroscopic surveillance streams, the network estimates a regularization-guided, constraint-dependent set of seven phenomenological effective fractional orders rather than genuine biological memory parameters. In the reference run, inferred compartment orders span approximately 0.688 to 0.864 (mean 0.753), whereas a single-head global-order model achieves identical reconstruction error (RMSE = 0.0028) and removing the diversity penalty contracts compartment means to between 0.740 and 0.774 (RMSE = 0.0021). Under regularization-guided optimization, the multi-head model captures nonlinear transitions in exposure and recovery alongside quasi-stationary institutional plateaus; this alignment reflects post hoc temporal coincidence with policy shifts rather than causality. Furthermore, the inferred regime yields a modest reduction of roughly 2% to 3% (1.38 to 1.35) in the definition-driven, phenomenological fractional reproduction metric. Because the explicit solver numerically constrains trajectories to the discretized governing dynamics, AlphaNet7 outperforms fixed-order baselines in calibration and out-of-sample forecasting, reducing forecast error by 30.2% to 63.1% across rolling hold-out splits under unified normalization. papers.title: Artificial-intelligence-assisted inverse design of low-carbon concrete under carbonation constraints
papers.abstract: This study develops and tests an artificial-intelligence-assisted inverse-design workflow for supplementary-cementitious-material-blended concrete, with artificial intelligence applied to surrogate prediction, uncertainty quantification, dosage-effect interpretation, and multi-objective candidate generation. Optuna-tuned feedforward neural networks were trained on four open datasets and coupled with split conformal prediction, continuous-treatment forest analysis, and non-dominated multi-objective search. The source-aware compressive-strength model achieved a mean absolute error of 7.20 megapascals and a coefficient of determination of 0.687. Under standard cross-validation, embodied carbon achieved a mean absolute error of 2.41 and a coefficient of determination of 0.999, while carbonation depth achieved a mean absolute error of 2.56 millimetres and a coefficient of determination of 0.847. A leakage audit showed that the exceptional embodied-carbon fit is largely attributable to an almost deterministic relation between mixture quantities and the carbon target, although performance was sensitive to source grouping. Continuous-treatment re-analysis showed substantial pre-adjustment imbalance and wide ninety-five-percent effect intervals, so the dosage results are interpreted conditionally rather than as universal causal effects. Three-objective optimization produced seventy-two computational candidates; sixteen, or 22.2 percent, had negative raw carbonation predictions and were excluded from representative reporting. A physically non-negative balanced candidate predicted 75.8 megapascals strength, 141.7 embodied carbon, and 0.064 millimetres carbonation depth. Applicability-domain analysis showed that none of the optimized candidates lay inside a strict joint ninety-five-percent domain for all retained endpoints, emphasizing that the generated mixtures are hypotheses for laboratory validation rather than design-ready prescriptions.

papers.title: NN-Based Approach to Model Predictive Control for Three-Phase Inverters Using One- or Two-Step Horizons
papers.abstract: Finite-control-set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) gives low-distortion voltage regulation for LC-filtered two-level three-phase inverters, but its computation grows exponentially with the prediction horizon. We trained neural networks offline to imitate it. Four imitators were formed by crossing two network types, a pattern-recognition classifier (NNPR) and a regression network (NNRG), with data from one-step and two-step FCS-MPC teacher controllers, giving NNPR1, NNPR2, NNRG1, and NNRG2. All were evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink with linear resistive loads at sixteen training and four unseen interpolated conditions. Mean output-voltage total harmonic distortion (THD) was 2.55% for NNPR1, 0.89% for NNPR2, 2.89% for NNRG1, and 1.36% for NNRG2, against 2.32% and 1.73% for one-step and two-step FCS-MPC, respectively. The training horizon mattered more than the network type, and the classifier gave lower mean THD at both horizons. NNPR2 gave lower THD than its teacher controller at all sixteen conditions while switching 26% less often. The advantage came mainly from the load current, which the teacher controller estimated but the networks received as measured; given the measured value, the teacher controller came within 0.13 percentage points of NNPR2. Network computation is horizon-independent; MATLAB execution times are indicative only. Results are simulation-only; hardware-in-the-loop validation with delay compensation must precede deployment.

papers.title: Equilibrium-Consistent Reservoir Prediction and Risk-Adaptive Model Predictive Control for Nonlinear Wing-Flutter Suppression
papers.abstract: We investigate equilibrium-consistent reservoir-computing (RC) prediction and adaptively weighted model predictive control (MPC) for a nonlinear pitch–plunge flutter benchmark at Qf=8. A conditional residual-mean network compensates for RC prediction errors, and a post-training correction enforces the known zero equilibrium. The optimizer uses deterministic corrected-mean prediction; K-nearest-neighbor (KNN) residual-error covariance adjusts state and terminal penalties, without stochastic scenario propagation. Against separately tuned fixed weights, KNN-based weighting reduced normalized integral squared error (ISE) by 1.66% in a reference Gaussian-disturbance setting with five paired realizations. Four systematic noise conditions included independent and synthetic AR(1) disturbances. An additional exploratory comparison on two new paired Gaussian noise realizations used a fully KNN-independent state-feedback weight scheduler. This simpler scheduler lowered mean normalized ISE (0.151199 versus 0.155306 for KNN) but required more input effort (1.579680 versus 1.231068) and showed slightly larger late-stage normalized root mean square error (0.008832 versus 0.008410). Thus, the comparison exposes a regulation–effort trade-off but does not establish an incremental advantage specifically attributable to KNN covariance information. The KNN trace remains an empirical weighting signal rather than calibrated uncertainty. These results are limited to offline numerical simulations, without real-time or stochastic stability guarantees.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in University Physical Education Pedagogy: A Curriculum Framework for Vietnam
papers.abstract: Objectives. This review examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can support university physical education (PE) pedagogy and curriculum development while preserving motor learning, meaningful movement time, teacher judgment, safety, and equity, and proposes a context-sensitive framework for Vietnamese higher education. Materials and Methods. A structured narrative review and conceptual synthesis were conducted using peer-reviewed research and authoritative policy and guidance sources identified through PubMed and targeted scholarly searches of journal and publisher platforms. The search was updated on 23 September 2026. Priority was given to systematic and scoping reviews, recent empirical studies, and PE-focused sources addressing motor learning, movement analysis, feedback, assessment, wearables, teacher competence, ethics, and governance. Thirty-four sources were retained: 29 peer-reviewed journal articles and reviews and five policy or guidance documents. Coding and theory-driven consolidation were used to map recurring findings to framework elements, with greater interpretive weight given to reviews and authoritative guidance. Results. Five application domains were identified: curriculum needs analysis and learning design, personalized motor-learning support, movement recognition and feedback, multimodal movement and participation monitoring, and teacher and program support. Educational value depended on context-specific validity, teacher competence, data governance, equitable access, and preservation of active learning time. The proposed AI-PE framework links six components—learning outcomes, learner data, learning design, AI support, multi-source assessment, and curriculum improvement—under three safeguards: human decision-making, data safety and ethics, and equitable access. Conclusions. AI should function as a pedagogical and decision-support layer rather than an autonomous instructor or assessor. The framework places embodied learning, motor competence, physical activity, and teacher responsibility at the center and provides a basis for institutional pilots and empirical validation in Vietnamese universities.

papers.title: A hybrid uncertainty-aware deep learning framework for reliable Malayalam fake news detection
papers.abstract: Fake news detection in low resource languages like Malayalam is a challenging task due to linguistic complexity, limited linguistic resources and lack of annotated datasets. The deep learning models has proven good impact in text classification tasks, but they lack reliability and interpretability that are critical for real world deployment. There are some recent studies that focus on explainable artificial intelligence to interpret model predictions but the reliability of these explanations under uncertain predictions has not been addressed. This paper proposes an uncertainty aware framework for Malayalam fake news detection using different deep learning architectures, including Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), CNN-LSTM, Bidirectional GRU (BiGRU), CNN-GRU, and CNN-BiLSTM. Four uncertainty estimation techniques Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout, Deep Ensemble Learning, Test Time Augmentation (TTA) and Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) are used and compared with baseline models. Along with fake news classification, the proposed framework quantifies predictive uncertainty through entropy, Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, mutual information, variance, and vacuity measures, enabling the identification of unreliable predictions. A hybrid uncertainty framework combining MC Dropout, Deep Ensemble Learning and Evidential Learning is proposed to jointly capture epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty while providing a complementary evidence based uncertainty estimates. The proposed hybrid framework achieves an accuracy of 96.51%, precision of 96.52%, recall of 96.51%, and F1-score of 96.51%. To assess the robustness of proposed hybrid model result and address variability due to random initialization, an additional five-seed experiment was conducted. The Hybrid model achieved an accuracy of 95.85 ± 0.18, precision of 95.85 ± 0.18%, recall of 95.85 ± 0.18%, and F1-score of 95.85 ± 0.18%, indicating stable performance across multiple runs. Furthermore, the calibration analysis demonstrates substantial improvements in prediction reliability, achieving the lowest Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 0.0066, Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) of 0.1014, and Brier Score of 0.0546 among all evaluated models. The five seed experiment achieved an ECE of ( $$0.0067 \pm 0.0023$$ ), MCE ( $$0.0955 \pm 0.0494$$ ), NLL ( $$0.1229 \pm 0.0027$$ ), and Brier score ( $$0.0659 \pm 0.0007$$ ) for the proposed hybrid model, which is lower than all other models. Although the Deep Ensemble and MC Dropout + Ensemble models achieve slightly higher mean classification accuracy, the proposed Hybrid Model achieves the lowest ECE, MCE, NLL, and Brier score across the five-seed experiments, indicating improved calibration and probabilistic prediction quality. Additional evaluation using uncertainty specific metrics such as Uncertainty Accuracy Coefficient (UAC), Uncertainty Precision Ratio (UPR), Uncertainty Sensitivity Estimate (USE), and Uncertainty Specificity Percentage (USP) confirms the effectiveness of the proposed framework in identifying uncertain predictions while maintaining high classification performance. The experimental evaluations demonstrates that uncertainty aware models provide better calibration and improved reliability compared to baseline architectures while maintaining competitive classification performance. The results shows that the hybrid uncertainty modeling effectively reduces overconfidence and enhances trustworthiness by distinguishing between confident and uncertain samples, that highlights the importance of uncertainty quantification in low resource language fake news detection.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Time-Dependent Moderate Reynolds Flow Around a Rotating Cylinder: A Study of Lift, Drag, and Wake Dynamics
papers.abstract: This study assesses physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for the unsteady two-dimensional flow past a rotating circular cylinder confined in a channel (blockage ratio 0.2) at Reynolds numbers of 50, 200 and 500. The networks are trained on the non-dimensional Navier–Stokes residuals, the boundary conditions including the rotating wall, and an initial velocity field, using adaptive loss weighting and time marching. A finite-volume reference solver, verified against the Schäfer–Turek benchmark to within 1.2%, is used to quantify the PINN accuracy and to characterise the flow for rotation ratios between −1 and 1.5. Rotation produces a Magnus lift that increases almost linearly with the rotation ratio (Cl¯≈−3.7α), reduces the mean drag and leaves the Strouhal number nearly unchanged, while all cases, including the stationary cylinder at Re=50, exhibit periodic vortex shedding. The data-free PINN reproduces the wake topology and the sign of the Magnus lift, with relative L2 velocity errors of 14–24%, but underestimates the pressure and the hydrodynamic forces. A systematic ablation shows that sparse velocity data (0.4% of the domain) halve the velocity error, and that a hard rotating-wall constraint with boundary-layer sampling further reduces it to 6% and lowers the lift error to 30% at Re=50. The persistent force errors at higher Reynolds numbers identify the representation of the thin rotating boundary layer as the principal limitation of PINNs for this class of flows.

papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate identification of ship maneuvering model parameters plays a critical role in ship motion control, navigation safety, and intelligent decision-making. However, the nonlinear and strongly coupled characteristics of ship dynamics render traditional identification methods difficult to apply under limited or noisy data conditions. To address these challenges, a self-adaptive physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework is proposed in this study, in which the governing equations of ship motion are coupled to formulate a multidimensional loss function and a scalable hyperparameter is embedded into the activation function to dynamically adjust the loss function landscape during training, thereby enhancing the prediction accuracy and convergence speed of ship maneuvering performance. The method is validated through parameter identification experiments using ± 20 ° zigzag maneuver simulation data of a Mariner-class vessel. The proposed adaptive-activation PINN method significantly reduces the identification errors of several key maneuvering parameters under limited sampling and noise-contaminated conditions, demonstrating higher accuracy and robustness. This study can provide dynamic support for intelligent navigation decision-making and optimal control, which is conducive to achieving high-precision control and decision optimization for autonomous ships in complex sea conditions.

papers.title: Model-Based Q-Learning for Dynamic Cache Allocation in Multi-Tenant Edge Computing
papers.abstract: In multi-tenant edge computing, several Service Providers (SPs) share a limited cache. Because the traffic demand of each SP changes over time, a fixed cache partition can leave space unused for one SP while another SP suffers cache misses and longer response delay. This paper proposes a dynamic cache allocation framework that monitors the traffic demand and cache usage of every SP and moves unused cache space to the SPs that need it. Allocation decisions are supported by model-based reinforcement learning (MB-RL) built on Q-learning. A regression model estimates cost or performance from system conditions, experience replay reuses past experiences during learning, and an epsilon-greedy policy balances trying new actions with choosing learned ones. Every candidate action is checked against two hard rules before it is applied: the total allocation must not exceed the cache capacity, and every SP must keep a minimum cache share. Fair sharing is therefore enforced by construction rather than left to the learning signal. The paper presents the system architecture, the allocation procedure, a worked example with a 100 GB cache, and a planned evaluation based on cache utilization, response delay, cache hit ratio, and fairness. The framework is expected to improve cache usage, reduce unnecessary cache misses and response delay, and support fair sharing among tenants compared with fixed allocation.

papers.title: Forecasting irrigation water requirement driven by meteorological forecast error correction in the Yellow River irrigation area of Shandong Province
papers.abstract: Irrigation water requirement (IWR) is a key parameter in agro-hydrological research and water resource optimization. Its forecast accuracy determines irrigation scheduling reliability, but it is constrained by meteorological errors, which propagate through the modeling chain. An optimal correction scheme was developed for short-term (1–3 days), medium-term (4–15 days), and long-term (16–40 days) forecasts of maximum temperature (T′ max ), minimum temperature (T′ min ), and precipitation (P′) based on 1–40-day public weather forecasts from 2019 to 2023. A regionally calibrated Hargreaves model was evaluated for estimating reference evapotranspiration (ET o ), and an IWR forecast method driven by meteorological error correction was established. The results demonstrate that optimal correction methods varied by lead time: the decaying-average method based on autocorrelation function (ACF-DAM) was optimal for T′ max at short lead times; genetic algorithm (GA)-optimized long short-term memory (LSTM) for T′ max at medium-to-long lead times and T′ min at short-to-medium lead times; stepwise regression (SR) for T′ min at long lead times; and Bayesian optimization (BO)-optimized random forest (RF) for P′ across all lead times. ET o forecasts achieved accuracy exceeding 80% at 86.36% of stations across different lead times. ET o predicti o ns ranged from 2.06 to 3.48 mm d −1 , with root mean square error (RMSE) values of 1.22 mm d −1 (short-term), 0.87–0.99 mm d −1 (medium-term), and 1.25–1.32 mm d −1 (long-term). Spatially, the Yellow River Delta and northern plains performed best, while the central region showed larger errors. Across different lead times, IWR forecasts remained stable, with IWR ranging from 145.13 to 293.62 mm for winter wheat and from 31.34 to 239.99 mm for summer maize; station-mean values were 207.11–249.39 mm and 78.21–196.69 mm, respectively. Spatially, IWR was higher in the north and lower in the southwest. Correcting weather forecast errors can significantly reduce the prediction errors of ET o , ET c , and IWR, providing a scientific basis for hydrological regulation, water allocation, and agricultural water demand forecasting in irrigation districts.

papers.abstract: Educational resource allocation requires the simultaneous consideration of regional demand heterogeneity, spatial adjacency, and nonlinear prediction relationships. This study presents an integrated framework that combines Spatially Constrained Entropy-Weighted K-Means (SCEW-KMeans) with Bayesian Optimization–Random Forest (BO-RF). SCEW-KMeans employs entropy weights to quantify the informational heterogeneity of indicators related to educational supply, population demand, and fiscal capacity, incorporates county-level spatial adjacency into the clustering objective function, and identifies stable regional partitions through Bootstrap consensus selection. During the demand forecasting stage, a nested spatial block cross-validation strategy is adopted, with Linear Regression (LR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Global Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) serving as unified competitive benchmark models. Experimental results based on annual observational data from 95 county-level administrative units in Jiangsu Province from 2021 to 2023 demonstrated that the SCEW-KMeans and BO-RF joint framework achieved a mean squared error (MSE) of 94.9 and a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.879 in predicting county-level per-student fiscal expenditure on education. The clustering results attain an average silhouette coefficient of 0.65, a Bootstrap-Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) of 0.91, and a spatial boundary cut ratio of 0.18.

papers.title: A Topological and Geometric Framework for the Transformation from Graphene to Toroidal Carbon Nanotubes
papers.abstract: We develop a unified geometric and topological framework to describe the transformation of planar graphene into cylindrical and toroidal carbon nanotubes while maintaining strict consistency with graphene's lattice structure and low-energy Dirac electronic theory. Starting from the continuum approximation of graphene, we construct cylindrical and toroidal compactifications through lattice-compatible boundary identifications and analyze the corresponding evolution of the fundamental group. For the toroidal case, we explicitly classify flat U(1) gauge connections via holonomy representations of the fundamental group, demonstrating the existence of two independent flux parameters defined modulo the flux quantum. We derive the momentum quantization conditions directly from Dirac spinor boundary compatibility with the underlying lattice and valley structure, avoiding heuristic plane-wave assumptions. The mechanical stability of the toroidal geometry is shown to follow from the Helfrich bending energy, whose small-deformation limit yields the curvature-dependent functional used in our analysis, and we further verify this stability through the eigenvalue spectrum of the bending operator. By formulating the Dirac Hamiltonian on a curved surface, we demonstrate that curvature induces an effective geometric gauge field through the spin connection, leading to a curvature-dependent modification of the quantization condition. The resulting unified quantization law incorporates lattice periodicity, electromagnetic flux, and geometric curvature on equal footing. We illustrate the framework with a graphene-scale numerical example, a doubly-quantized Dirac spectrum for representative metallic and semiconducting toroidal configurations, and a comparison with experimentally observed toroidal carbon nanotubes, and we discuss the embedding and mechanical-stability constraints that separate topologically valid but physically unrealistic configurations from experimentally realizable nanotori. This framework provides a mathematically consistent description of toroidal carbon nanotubes as compact, doubly-periodic quantum systems and clarifies the interplay between topology, curvature, and electronic structure in curved graphene-based nanostructures.

papers.title: Enhanced biogas production via dual‐layer model predictive control for thermophilic anaerobic digesters
papers.abstract: Abstract Thermophilic anaerobic digestion (AD) is an attractive process due to its higher biogas yield compared to mesophilic digestion. To mitigate its higher heating demand and potential process instability, a dual‐layer control architecture comprising a decision‐making layer and an adaptive model predictive control (MPC) system is proposed. Two specific supervisory layers are designed for startup and demand‐oriented phases. First, a gain‐scheduling supervisory layer generates a trajectory that ensures a smooth transition to steady‐state operation. Second, a demand‐oriented supervisory layer is developed to align biogas conversion into combined heat and power (CHP) with the grid requirements, employing an optimization framework. The underlying MPC layer utilizes an adaptive linear input‐output model to track optimal trajectories while rejecting disturbances. Furthermore, a circular design is integrated wherein the controller stimulates additional biogas production to satisfy internal heating requirements. Simulation results demonstrate that the control system enhances the process performance.

papers.title: Mechanical Durability of Contemporary Dental Materials: An Engineering Review and Research Roadmap
papers.abstract: Dental restorations and implants operate under coupled cyclic loading, contact, sliding, moisture, thermal fluctuation, saliva chemistry and manufacturing-induced defects; therefore, static strength alone is an inadequate predictor of service life. This critical review synthesizes 50 peer-reviewed studies published in 2025-2026 and interprets zirconia/glass-ceramics, resin composites and additively manufactured polymers, PEEK/highperformance polymers, and titanium/Co-Cr systems through a process-structure-property-environment-life framework. Evidence shows that build orientation, layer thickness, firing or post-curing, milling, surface treatment and ageing alter defect populations and fatigue reliability; printed-resin durability remains protocol-dependent; and implant performance requires simultaneous treatment of micromotion, stress redistribution, corrosion and tribocorrosion. The review integrates service-representative testing, fracture/fatigue and wear metrics, reliability analysis and validated finite-element modelling into a compact experimental-computational methodology. Priority directions are standardized fatigue/wear protocols, defect-informed additive-manufacturing models, calibrated ageing, coupled bio-tribocorrosion-fatigue testing, experimentally validated probabilistic FEA, and multi objective material-process-geometry optimization.

papers.title: Gaussian Process Modelling for Precision Olive Irrigation-Fertilization Management: Continuous Prediction and Uncertainty Quantification of Olive Oil Quality
papers.abstract: Introduction Olive oil quality is influenced by irrigation, fertilization, and seasonal climate variability. This study aimed to predict quality at unobserved water-fertilizer combinations while quantifying predictive uncertainty for risk-informed management. Methods A two-year (2023-2024) split-plot 3×3 factorial trial at INRA Meknès, Morocco, generated 54 biological olive-oil samples of Olea europaea L. cv. Picholine Marocaine across nine water-fertilizer combinations (50-100% ETc × 50-100% NPK), yielding 324 FTIR-ATR acquisitions. Matérn-5/2 Gaussian Process models with Automatic Relevance Determination were trained on 18 treatment-year means. Performance was assessed using Spearman ρ 2 under leave-one-treatment-out and leave-one-year-out cross-validation. Uncertainty was partitioned into aleatoric, temporal, and epistemic components, and Pareto optimisation identified resource-efficient regimes. Results LOTO-CV ρ 2 ranged from 0.408 (TFC) to 0.750 (carotenoids), with DPPH at 0.633 and TPC at 0.427. LOYO ρ 2 reached 0.790 for carotenoids and 0.494 for TPC. Temporal uncertainty accounted for ~58% of total uncertainty, versus 36% aleatoric and 6% epistemic. TPC was more sensitive to irrigation than fertilization (W/F = 0.22). The Pareto-optimal regime (≈50% ETc × ≈56% NPK) achieved 91% of maximum composite quality with 28% lower fertilisation cost. Discussion Seasonal variability was the dominant uncertainty source, highlighting the importance of multi-year data. Carotenoid and TPC patterns transferred across seasons, whereas DPPH required seasonal recalibration. Conclusion FTIR-GP modelling with Pareto optimisation offers a promising framework for uncertainty-aware olive management, but broader validation across seasons, sites, and cultivars is needed.

papers.title: A GNN-Enhanced PINN Framework Driven by Constrained Graph-Point Coupling for Two-Dimensional Material Wavefield Propagation
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have difficulty fully exploiting discrete spatial neighborhood information, while conventional graph neural networks (GNNs) cannot readily compute higher-order partial derivatives directly at arbitrary continuous collocation points. To address these challenges, this study proposes a GNN-enhanced PINN framework based on constrained graph-to-point coupling for two-dimensional wavefield propagation in materials. The framework uses a PINN to represent the continuous base wavefield and a GNN to extract local spatial information. Interpolation, constrained residual correction, and learnable gating are integrated into the graph-to-point coupling process, combining discrete graph representations with continuous physical constraints while preserving the initial boundary compatibility of the correction. A two-dimensional wave benchmark in a homogeneous medium shows that, compared with a baseline PINN, the framework reduces full space–time prediction errors and improves predictions of propagating wavefronts and boundary-reflection structures. These results provide a feasible approach to material wavefield solution that combines spatial neighborhood information with continuous physical constraints.

papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The level of femoral neck resection in total hip arthroplasty (THA) affects implant position, restoration of limb length, and degree of cortical support available for collared cementless stems. With increasing use of computed tomography (CT)-based planning and collared stems, understanding femoral neck and calcar morphology at the osteotomy plane is valuable. The aims of this study were to (1) quantify femoral neck cortical thickness at the achieved osteotomy plane reconstructed from postoperative imaging and adjacent levels, (2) assess the effect of osteotomy height on regional cortical support, and (3) determine the medial collar length that best matches cortical thickness at the osteotomy plane. METHODS: We reviewed preoperative CT scans from 100 consecutive primary THAs performed by a single surgeon using a single cementless femoral stem design. Using multiplanar reconstruction, calcar cortical thickness was measured on axial images at the osteotomy plane (zero mm) and at standardized levels 5.30 mm proximal and 5.30 mm distal to that plane. At each level, thickness was recorded at five locations (anterior, posterior, medial, antero-medial, and postero-medial). The medial cortical thickness at the osteotomy plane was used to determine the collar length, minimizing absolute overhang/underhang, which corresponds to its median. RESULTS: Cortical thickness increased from proximal to distal levels, most prominently in the medial (P < 0.001) and postero-medial (P < 0.001) regions. Antero-medial thickness increased from the proximal level to the osteotomy plane (P = 0.004), but did not increase further distally (P = 0.641). For this cohort and osteotomy technique, the collar length minimizing mean absolute overhang or underhang was 5.3 mm, the median medial cortical thickness at the osteotomy plane. CONCLUSION: At and around the planned femoral neck osteotomy plane, medial and postero-medial cortices were thickest and increased in thickness distally, whereas antero-medial thickness plateaued. These data provide an anatomic reference that may inform cementless femoral stem collar geometry and future implant design.

papers.title: Experimental surrogate-based MPC of twin-screw extrusion from sparse measurements
papers.abstract: We demonstrate real-time surrogate-model-based temperature control of a co-rotating twin-screw extruder. A one-dimensional mechanistic extruder model describing mass transport, pressure dynamics, and heat transfer is extended and experimentally validated. To enable real-time optimization, neural network surrogate models in a nonlinear autoregressive with exogenous inputs formulation are trained on simulation data from the mechanistic model. Given the sparsity of available measurements, a surrogate is combined with a particle filter for robust state observation, reconstructing the complete melt and barrel temperature profiles from only three melt temperature sensors. A Bayesian optimization algorithm is proposed for optimal sensor placement that maximizes state observation accuracy under hardware constraints. A surrogate is integrated into a model predictive control formulation that simultaneously maximizes melt temperature, tracks throughput references, and enforces constraints imposed by material characteristics and process limitations for industrially relevant product cases. The complete closed-loop scheme is validated experimentally on a pilot-scale extrusion process.

papers.title: Digital Twin Technologies for Intelligent Monitoring, Predictive Maintenance, and Autonomous Decision Making in Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems: A Comprehensive Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to systematically review the current state of digital twin technologies in industrial cyber-physical systems and evaluate their roles in intelligent monitoring, predictive maintenance, and autonomous decision-making. It also sought to identify major architectural frameworks, enabling technologies, adoption barriers, and emerging directions for cognitive digital twins in industrial environments. Material and Methods: A structured systematic review methodology was applied using peer-reviewed literature published between 2020 and 2025. Searches were conducted across IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink using Boolean combinations of terms related to digital twins, industrial cyber-physical systems, intelligent monitoring, predictive maintenance, autonomous decision-making, and Industry 4.0/5.0. Studies were screened through title, abstract, and full-text review using defined inclusion and exclusion criteria, followed by thematic data extraction, quality assessment, and synthesis. Results: The review included 87 publications and identified five major themes: intelligent monitoring, predictive maintenance, autonomous decision-making, security and interoperability challenges, and future directions. Findings showed that digital twins improve operational visibility, reduce downtime, support fault prediction, and enable self-optimizing processes. Reported benefits included 30–50% reductions in unplanned downtime, 20–40% longer equipment life, and fault diagnosis accuracy of 97.3% in one energy case study. Conclusion: Digital twin technologies are becoming foundational for smarter, more resilient, and sustainable industrial systems, but wider adoption still depends on advances in standardization, security, scalability, interoperability, and organizational readiness

papers.title: Semi-analytical, physics-informed and numerical solution of a nonlinear reaction–diffusion biofilm model for the biofiltration of ethyl acetate and toluene as single pollutants and in mixture
papers.abstract: The biodegradation of volatile organic compounds inside a microbial biofilm is governed by the competition between diffusive transport and inhibited microbial consumption, yet the coupled ethyl-acetate–toluene–oxygen subsystem that controls this process has rarely been examined as a self-contained boundary-value problem. This study isolates the biofilm equations of a dynamic peat-biofilter model and analyses the steady-state, dimensionless reaction–diffusion balances of ethyl acetate, toluene and oxygen, incorporating Haldane self-inhibition of ethyl acetate, Monod kinetics for toluene, competitive cross-inhibition of toluene by ethyl acetate, and dual oxygen limitation of both substrates. The resulting coupled nonlinear system is solved by three independent routes: the semi-analytical Akbari–Ganji method (AGM), a physics-informed neural network (PINN), and a pdepe-based method-of-lines scheme adopted as the numerical benchmark. Mixture, ethyl-acetate-only and toluene-only configurations are each studied across five Thiele-modulus cases spanning reaction-controlled to strongly diffusion-limited regimes. A quantitative point-by-point error analysis shows that the PINN retains sub-0.15% relative error throughout, whereas the AGM is essentially exact at low modulus and deviates by up to about 2% in the film interior at high modulus. A normalized sensitivity analysis identifies oxygen diffusivity as the dominant control on biofilm effectiveness, followed by ethyl-acetate self-inhibition and competitive cross-inhibition. The results also expose a pronounced kinetic asymmetry in which cross-inhibition and shared oxygen demand shape the two substrate profiles in opposite directions.

papers.title: Temporal probabilistic soft sensing and constrained Bayesian recipe screening for semiconductor CMP processes
papers.abstract: Delayed metrology and changing process conditions make reliable material removal rate (MRR) prediction and recipe screening difficult in chemical–mechanical planarization (CMP). This study links temporal soft sensing, uncertainty calibration and constrained Bayesian screening within a reproducible manufacturing-data workflow. Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) predicts MRR from wafer–stage features; historical residuals provide a process-state uncertainty scale, and a disjoint chronological calibration window determines prediction intervals. A candidate-dependent residual Gaussian process (GP) ranks recipe proxies within a shared empirical feasible region. On 396 time-out observations, the point predictor achieved R2 = 0.9543 and root mean square error (RMSE) = 5.9743; the guarded 95% interval attained 95.96% empirical coverage. In 20 model-in-the-loop scenarios, the proposed method achieved a 95.0% target-window hit rate and generated feasible candidates throughout the evaluation budget. Constrained baselines attained the same final hit rate, identifying the contribution of shared feasibility screening. The framework supports uncertainty-aware CMP recipe pre-screening through temporally separated predictive validation and independent evaluator-based decision analysis.

papers.title: Avascular necrosis of the femur following COVID-19: an updated systematic review
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: One of the complications of COVID-19 infection is avascular necrosis of the femoral head. To date, various studies have reported a wide range of osteonecrosis of the femoral head in patients with COVID-19. The previous systematic review included only 14 studies. So, this systematic review aims to update the findings of these studies. METHODS: Databases such as PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were systematically searched by two independent researchers on April 1st, 2024. RESULTS: A literature search revealed 1229 records, 161 full-texts were evaluated, and finally, 55 studies remained for systematic review. Fifty-five studies were included in this systematic review. Four studies were cross-sectional studies, six were retrospective studies, and the remaining (45studies) were case reports or case-series studies. Totally, 864 cases were included. Except for 12 studies, 43 studies reported the administration of steroid therapy in included cases. The most common underlying conditions were hypertension, followed by diabetes. In 274 (31.7%) of included cases, AVN was bilateral, and both hips were involved. In some studies, non-surgical treatments-including supplement therapy, anticoagulant therapy, physiotherapy, and hyperbaric oxygen therapy-were administered. Several studies reported symptomatic improvement in patients treated with the core decompression approach. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) was the most commonly used surgical treatment. CONCLUSIONS: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head in cases that have survived COVID-19 should be considered carefully as early diagnosis helps to preserve the joint and its function.

papers.title: Manufacturing-Structure-Performance Engineering of Advanced Dental Materials: Additive Manufacturing, Surface Engineering and Computational Design
papers.abstract: Advanced dental materials are manufactured states whose performance depends on digital geometry, additive or subtractive processing, post-processing, surface modification, defects and oral loading. This focused critical review synthesizes 50 peer-reviewed publications from 2025–2026 using an explicitly documented search, eligibility, screening and evidence-coding protocol rather than a PRISMA systematic-review claim. The literature is integrated through a manufacturing–structure–performance (MSP) framework linking process variables to defect/microstructural and surface states and then to dimensional accuracy, fatigue, wear, adhesion and functional durability. Comparative synthesis shows that additive-manufacturing studies are strongest in static mechanical and accuracy characterization but weaker in defect-informed fatigue; surface-engineering evidence is increasingly multifunctional but coating durability is inconsistently tested; finite-element analysis is advancing toward patientspecific models but remains limited by idealized properties, contacts and experimental validation; and AI/ML is constrained by small, heterogeneous and weakly transferable datasets. A closed digital thread is proposed in which metrology and experiments calibrate predictive mechanics, validated simulations and tests generate traceable datasets, surrogate models accelerate prediction and multi-objective optimization identifies robust process/design windows. Priority directions include defect-informed zirconia AM, cure–conversion–fatigue modelling of printed resins, multifunctional coating durability, experimentally validated patient-specific FEA, inverse implant design, digital twins and sustainability-aware manufacturing optimization.

papers.title: A lightweight model for real-time safety management of nanoparticle concentrations in industrial spray processes
papers.abstract: Industrial spraying processes incidentally generate high rates of hazardous nanoparticles (NPs), posing significant health risks to workers. While ventilation systems are critical for mitigation, optimizing their operation via Model Predictive Control (MPC) requires fast predictive tools, making traditional Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) unsuitable due to high computational costs. This study develops and validates a physics-based Lightweight Model (LWM) designed to predict real-time NPs concentrations in a thermal spraying booth. Based on a multizone airflow approach, the LWM incorporates source emissions, airflows induced by ventilation and openings, and diffusive transport using a well-mixed mass balance formulation. The model was validated using experimental data from an industrial facility and benchmarked against detailed CFD simulations. Results demonstrate that the LWM accurately predicts both the transient growth and steady-state stabilization of NP concentrations, achieving comparable accuracy to CFD but with drastically reduced computation time (minutes versus days). By offering accurate predictions with minimal computational demand, the proposed LWM is a promising prediction model for future MPC-based occupational safety and ventilation control. Its implementation and validation within a complete MPC framework remain future work.

papers.title: Personalized Bone Tumor Treatment Sequencing Using Counterfactual Causal Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: The sequencing of treatment for patients with bone tumors is an acute issue because these tumors develop heterogeneously, their therapies interact in multiple ways, and the current AI-based clinical decision support systems do not understand the investigation of these tumors. Majority of the existing methods are based on correlation-based predictive models that do not reflect the actual effect of alternative treatment plans in the long-run. The proposed work develops a Counterfactual Causal Reinforcement Learning (CCRL) model framework to optimize bone tumor treatment in a personalized treatment. The model combines Structural Causal Models (SCM) to learn causal graphs, a counterfactual simulation engine to judge the hypothetical effects of treatment, and a deep reinforcement learning policy network to make an optimal decision. The training and validation are performed using multi-modal longitudinal datasets that include CT/MRI imaging, radiomic features, and clinical records. The experimental analysis shows that the proposed CCRL model can reach an accuracy of 98.94% in treatment response, a 21.3% enhance in decision optimality, and a 17.6% decrease in recurrence risk than traditional deep learning and RL-based baselines. The framework offers interpretable, evidence-based treatment suggestions that will enhance precision oncology by incorporating causal AI.

papers.title: Developing a conceptual model of mentorship‐guided instructional change
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Evidence‐based instructional practices, such as active learning and formative assessment, are recognized for their ability to significantly improve student learning outcomes in engineering education. However, widespread adoption of instructional change is often limited due to various barriers that faculty face, such as institutional resistance, lack of resources, and insufficient guidance. Purpose This study explores a course‐specific mentorship program designed to support engineering faculty in overcoming these barriers and fostering instructional change. The goal of this exploration is to construct a conceptual model of how mentorship programs can facilitate the adoption of innovative practices and address challenges faculty encounter. Design/Method A constructivist grounded theory approach was employed, using semi‐structured interviews with 26 mentees and 8 mentors to develop a conceptual model based on their experiences. Findings The resulting conceptual model articulates the adoption of innovative practices across three interconnected phases: Readiness, the Implementation Cycle, and Integration. Findings illustrate that instructional change is inherently nonlinear and iterative, with embedded mentor support—including tailored resource provision, collaboration, and structured reflection—enabling faculty to navigate classroom obstacles and achieve sustained adoption. Implications This study highlights the importance of targeted mentorship programs in bridging the awareness‐to‐practice gap in instructional change. By offering course‐specific guidance, mentorship programs can enhance faculty development and foster sustained implementation of innovative practices.

papers.abstract: Abstract Active learning methods, such as problem‐based learning (PBL), have been identified as effective strategies for developing interpersonal skills essential to professional practice. This study investigated the satisfaction, acceptance, and intention to continue using PBL by students in the Beekeeping course, as well as the main challenges faced with this approach at a Brazilian public university. Questionnaires were administered over four consecutive years (2022–2025). The instrument included demographic questions, Rosenberg's Self‐Esteem Scale to define the participants' self‐esteem profile, Likert scale statements to identify perceptions about the methodology, and open‐ended questions to identify challenges and suggestions for improvement. The results indicated high levels of satisfaction with PBL and a perception of improvement in problem‐solving skills. Students showed a preference for the methodology over traditional teaching, although they did not want its complete replacement. Gender was associated with differences in 17 of the 21 items evaluated, with men reporting more positive perceptions than women across all significant items, particularly regarding the perceived relevance of PBL for professional training, the item with the largest effect size in the study ( H = 20.39, p < .001, ε 2 = .144). Self‐esteem was associated with differences in 12 of the 21 items, with students with low self‐esteem consistently reporting less favorable perceptions than those with high self‐esteem. Among the main challenges reported were communication between peers and collective planning of solutions. PBL is a promising approach for teaching beekeeping in undergraduate courses, favoring the development of interpersonal skills relevant to professional practice.

papers.title: Architected Bio‐Based Iontronic Skin With Dual‐Mode Pressure and Strain Sensing
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human skin encodes pressure and stretch through the motion of ions, a principle soft iontronics reproduce but rarely on sustainable terms. Additive manufacturing has lifted ionogels from cast slabs into architected sensors, yet this progress rests on fossil‐derived acrylates, because plant‐based networks expel the polar ionic liquids that carry charge. Here we print an ionogel whose matrix exceeds 80% bio‐based carbon while stably hosting a hydrophobic imidazolium ionic liquid, resolving a long‐standing compatibility barrier. A single monomer ratio tunes stiffness 30 fold (9 to 0.3 MPa) and nearly doubles ionic conductivity to 0.53 mS cm −1 . Printed as gyroid lattices, the material senses pressure capacitively and strain resistively through separable channels: near‐incompressibility pins the gauge factor near 2 irrespective of geometry, whereas the lattice amplifies low‐pressure sensitivity eightfold and accelerates the strain response 4.6‐fold. On the body, both modes track joint motion with complementary signatures. Chemistry and printed architecture thus act as independent levers for renewable iontronic skin.

papers.abstract: This research sought to: 1) explore the existing and aspirational states of, and methodologies for, teacher development regarding the utilization of artificial intelligence (AI) for active learning within the Khon Kaen Primary Educational Service Area Office 2; 2) formulate a teacher development framework for the incorporation of AI into active learning; 3) assess the results of applying the formulated framework; and (4) enhance and authenticate the framework. The research utilized a Research and Development (R&D) approach comprising four stages. In Phase 1, the cohort consisted of 305 individuals, comprising 31 educational administrators and 274 educators active in the 2024 academic year, chosen via stratified random sampling. Furthermore, nine specialists participated in determining suitable methods for teacher improvement. During Phase 2, a total of 15 specialists contributed to the formulation of the model, and an additional nine experts assessed its quality. In Phase 3, the model was executed with 87 third-grade educators, including 53 from Ban Phai District and 34 from Chonnabot District, chosen by purposive sampling. During Phase 4, the identical cohort of educators engaged in reflection and satisfaction evaluation. The research tools included surveys, interview guidelines, assessment forms, and performance exams. The survey produced an Index of Item-Objective Congruence (IOC) of 0.98 and a reliability coefficient of 0.95. The interview process exhibited an IOC of 0.87, whereas the recognized components and indicators demonstrated an IOC of 0.90. The analysis of data was conducted using the mean, standard deviation, IOC, Modified Priority Needs Index (PNI_modified), dependent-samples t-test, and content analysis. The results indicated that: 1) the present state was at a diminished level, whereas the aspirational state was at an elevated level. The cumulative PNI_modified score was 0.79, with the cultivation of AI-related competencies seen as the foremost priority. The teacher development guidelines included four elements: crafting and strategizing active learning, structuring learner-centric activities, promoting cognitive processes and advanced skills, and executing genuine learning assessments; 2) the formulated model encompassed five aspects: principles, goals, developmental processes, assessment and evaluation, and prerequisites for effective implementation. The model received the utmost ratings for its suitability and practicality, and a commendable rating for its usefulness; 3) after the model's deployment, educators exhibited markedly enhanced knowledge and comprehension compared to their prior participation in the development program. Their average scores rose from 12.29 to 27.63 out of a maximum of 30, t(86) = 58.11,p < .001. Additionally, the educators successfully crafted lesson plans and executed AI-enhanced active learning at an optimal standard; furthermore, the instructors expressed maximum contentment with the model. The model was later endorsed by the Director of the Khon Kaen Primary Educational Service Area Office 2 along with five specialists, who affirmed its precision, suitability, and practical use for execution.

Design: Quasi-experimental research. Methods: The sample was selected using purposive sampling and consisted of 12 registered nurses and 66 older patients receiving intravenous fluids and medications. The older patients were equally assigned to the control group (n = 33) and the experimental group (n = 33). The research instruments consisted of: (1) data collection instruments, including demographic data forms, a knowledge questionnaire, a nursing practice observation checklist, and a phlebitis incidence record; (2) an intervention instrument, namely the nursing practice guideline for the prevention of peripheral intravenous phlebitis; and (3) intervention monitoring instruments, including a peripheral intravenous catheter insertion record and an intravenous fluid and medication administration record. papers.title: ForPC: Force-Aware Whole-Body Control for Precise Humanoid Cart Pushing
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots are expected to take over strenuous material handling in manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare, where operating existing wheeled carts would let them move heavy loads without modifying the workplace. However, humanoid cart pushing remains challenging because the bimanual grasp closes a force-coupled loop in which the contact wrenches that drive the cart also disturb the robot's balance, and payload changes alter the coupled dynamics. We propose ForPC, a force-aware whole-body control framework that regulates cart velocity through two-stage reinforcement learning. A locomotion prior is first trained under varied hand loads and upper-body postures to provide balance support. A force latent and a state latent are then inferred from onboard observations, without external force sensors, and fed to a residual policy that coordinates bounded arm, waist, and leg adjustments with base-velocity commands. Multi-objective rewards penalize bimanual internal opposition, grasp slip, and actuator saturation, encouraging the policy to apply contact force on demand without human demonstrations. Sim-to-sim experiments show that ForPC reduces cart-velocity RMSE by up to 68.2% relative to a locomotion-only baseline (Loco-only) and cross-track RMSE by up to 74.2% on the multi-bend route. Trained solely in simulation, the policy also transfers to a physical Unitree G1 without real-world training or fine-tuning and, with no payload-specific adjustment, pushes a cart carrying up to 30 kg at 0.5 m/s. These results suggest that humanoid robots could eventually replace humans for efficient material handling in daily life.

papers.title: Q-OIL: Optimistic Exploration in Learning from Human Interventions
papers.abstract: As robots are deployed in the real world, they will inevitably make mistakes. Human interventions provide valuable feedback for improving their behavior, enabling them to adapt online to new scenarios. However, studying human-in-the-loop robot learning is difficult: real-world experiments are slow and expensive, so most algorithm development relies on simulated human models. We show that common human modeling assumptions do not match how real people intervene in practice. Through analyzing intervention data from human participants, we find that humans tend to intervene when agent progress stalls, and that their corrective actions are often suboptimal. Motivated by these findings, we introduce a progress-based model of human intervention that achieves higher rank correlation with real-user algorithm rankings, enabling realistic algorithm benchmarking and development in simulation. Building on these insights, we propose Q-OIL, a method that adds optimistic bonuses to intervention transitions in reinforcement learning and softly guides exploration toward human corrections. We find that decoupled critics are critical for stability because they prevent the bonuses from backing up to pre-intervention states. As a result, Q-OIL learns more efficiently than competitive baselines, achieving 10-50% higher success in simulation and on real robots, and improving pretrained VLAs on two bimanual manipulation tasks. As we ground both evaluation and algorithms in realistic human behavior, this work provides a practical path toward scalable robot learning from interventions.

papers.title: Personalized health coaching via coachable health age and counterfactual wearable trajectories
papers.abstract: Personalized health coaching requires moving beyond retrospective wearable summaries toward quantitative, actionable behavioral prescriptions. We introduce Coachable Health Age (CHA), an interpretable health-age metric built from modifiable physiological and behavioral signals passively captured by consumer wearables. Across the WEAR-ME (N=2,780), All of Us (N=22,748), and longitudinal Fitbit (N=1,464) cohorts, CHA aligns with established cardiometabolic health constructs and improves prognostic discrimination for incident cardiovascular and metabolic disease beyond age, sex, and body mass index. To enable prospective behavioral optimization, we developed Sensor World Model (SensorWM), an action-conditioned wearable world model pretrained on over 2.2 million person-weeks of longitudinal sensor data from approximately 100,000 participants. SensorWM accurately forecasts multi-week physiological responses to candidate lifestyle changes ($R^2=0.664$), outperforming generic time-series foundation models while preserving downstream clinical signal for diabetes, hypertension, and other health outcomes. Finally, we integrate CHA and SensorWM into an agentic counterfactual coaching system to synthesize personalized 12-week coaching plans. In blinded paired reviews, certified lifestyle coaches preferred counterfactual-grounded plans over plans grounded in wearable history alone for overall quality (71.4%, P < 0.001) and anticipated adherence (71.0%, P < 0.001), and board-certified clinicians judged 99.2% of counterfactual-grounded plans to meet clinical safety criteria (vs. 97.6% of comparison plans). Automated evaluations across the full cohort (N=2,780) also favored counterfactual-grounded plans. By closing the loop between longitudinal tracking, trajectory prediction, and counterfactual coaching, our framework provides a scalable path to systematically improve cardiometabolic health.

papers.title: PINNeval: A Comprehensive Evaluation Standard for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: The Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) literature has produced a rapidly expanding catalogue of methods. We divide a PINN training pipeline systematically into four components and observe that many existing benchmarks study these components in isolation. These components are domain-importance adaptation, loss balancing, neural network architecture, and optimization scheme. Moreover, the studies set the surrounding and not considered components of the pipeline to a minimal default that is no longer representative of current best practice approaches. Conclusions drawn under such conditions may not transfer to competitive pipelines. In this work, we propose a new evaluation protocol that (1) treats the four components as an integrated system; (2) crucially requires competitive implementations of the components not under investigation; (3) specifies the metrics and reporting format; and (4) is accompanied by structured documentation that ensures the traceability of evaluations across studies. Based on this comprehensive protocol, we release PINNpipe, an innovative JAX package containing 18 different methods from the current literature as well as nine efficiently implemented benchmark problems. Using PINNpipe, we illustrate our evaluation protocol in relation to established benchmark studies and report results that challenge common assumptions.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文提出PINN统一评测协议与JAX工具包，可迁移用于FEA代理模型中PINN方法的公平对比与选型。
llm.why_not_core: It benchmarks PINN training components on standard PDE problems only, with no biomedical or implant mechanics application, no surrogate-based design optimization, and no uncertainty quantification.

summary_zh.method: 将训练流程拆为四组件，提出集成式评测协议并发布含18种方法和9个基准问题的JAX工具包PINNpipe。
summary_zh.result: 按新协议复现既有基准，结果挑战了关于各组件作用的常见假设。
summary_zh.validation: 在九个标准PDE基准问题上进行数值对比实验。

summary_en.motivation: Existing PINN benchmarks isolate individual pipeline components under minimal defaults, so their conclusions may not hold for competitive full pipelines.
summary_en.method: The authors decompose PINN training into four components, define an integrated evaluation protocol with competitive baselines and reporting standards, and release the JAX-based PINNpipe package with 18 methods and nine benchmark problems.
summary_en.result: Re-evaluation under the proposed protocol reproduces prior benchmark studies and yields findings that contradict several commonly held assumptions about component contributions.
summary_en.validation: Numerical experiments across nine standard PDE benchmark problems using the released toolkit.
